title: Aṭala-tīrtha
summary: Aṭala-tīrtha lies west of Gopavana, and it is where Kṛṣṇa stopped to rest with His friends because He could go no further after eating so much.
body: Aṭala-tīrtha lies west of Gopavana, and it is where Kṛṣṇa stopped to rest with His friends because He could go no further after eating so much. The name Aṭala means immovable, and it refers to how Kṛṣṇa felt as immovable as the food in His overfull belly. The gopas had been fed by the brāhmaṇīs' wives with many rich dishes cooked in ghee, and Madhumaṅgala stopped even earlier on the road. The boys relaxed in the shade of the trees around this tīrtha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Aṭalavana
summary: Aṭalavana lies west of Gopavana, and Kṛṣṇa declared here that He was as immovable as the food in His overfull belly after the feast the brāhmaṇīs had given the boys.
body: Aṭalavana lies west of Gopavana, and Kṛṣṇa declared here that He was as immovable as the food in His overfull belly after the feast the brāhmaṇīs had given the boys. The boys rested in the shade around Aṭala-tīrtha, and some slept while others relived the feast. The forest also lies near the samādhi of Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa on the outskirts of Vṛndāvana village, where he answered a challenge from the Rāmānandī sect at Jaipur. Gauravana, named after Caitanya Mahāprabhu, lies north of Gopavana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bacchavana
summary: Bacchavana, also called Vatsavana, lies next to Barifā and is where the boys once arrived empty-handed and extremely hungry after eating all their lunch.
body: Bacchavana, also called Vatsavana, lies next to Barifā and is where the boys once arrived empty-handed and extremely hungry after eating all their lunch. The cows were content to graze, but the gopas could not forget their hunger. Devotional accounts describe how, after the gopas ate their fill, they still had as much as when they had started, which Kṛṣṇa attributed to Lord Nārāyaṇa's mercy.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bahulā-kuṇḍa
summary: Bahulā-kuṇḍa is also called Māna-sarovara, since Rādhā sulked by the banks of Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa here until Kṛṣṇa won her over with the help of Her friends.
body: Bahulā-kuṇḍa is also called Māna-sarovara, since Rādhā sulked by the banks of Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa here until Kṛṣṇa won her over with the help of Her friends. It is called Bahulā-kuṇḍa because Bahulā attained perfection in this lake. Great devotees such as Jāhnavā-devī bathed here, since a visit to Bahulāvana would otherwise be incomplete without it. The dhāma's grace can bestow all perfection.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Baka-sthala
summary: Baka-sthala is a lake in Khadiravana near Nandīśvara, where Kṛṣṇa and His young friends took their calves from Chaṭīkarā to drink.
body: Baka-sthala is a lake in Khadiravana near Nandīśvara, where Kṛṣṇa and His young friends took their calves from Chaṭīkarā to drink. Kaṁsa had sent the demon Bakāsura to devour Kṛṣṇa, and the demon knew the boys' destination by mystic power. The demon sat upon the lake's water and opened his mouth wide, looking like a mountain with a gaping cave.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Balabhadra-kuṇḍa
summary: Balabhadra-kuṇḍa is on the road from Vṛndāvana town to Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and Baḍa-baṭhain lies a little to the south, where girls strike boys with bamboo sticks the day after Holī.
body: Balabhadra-kuṇḍa is on the road from Vṛndāvana town to Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and Baḍa-baṭhain lies a little to the south, where girls strike boys with bamboo sticks the day after Holī. The Balarāma Deity at Rāl, installed by King Vajranābha, is still worshipped on the bank of this lake. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma regularly went to this area with Their friends to tend the calves and play. The Gosvāmīs also met nearby under the shelter of Sevā-kuñja.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Balabhadravana
summary: Balabhadravana is one of the great forests (adhivanas) of New Vraja-dhāma, located at Baladeva.
body: Balabhadravana is one of the great forests (adhivanas) of New Vraja-dhāma, located at Baladeva. Traditional accounts list it among the forty-eight main forests and notes that another eighty-nine forests are also described. It appears mainly in lists of forests.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Baladeva-kuṇḍa
summary: Baladeva-kuṇḍa is a large lake on the outskirts of Mathurā City where Nanda Mahārāja and the Vraja-vāsīs camped during their stay.
body: Baladeva-kuṇḍa is a large lake on the outskirts of Mathurā City where Nanda Mahārāja and the Vraja-vāsīs camped during their stay. While they were there, Kṛṣṇa lived at this camp and made daily trips into the city to break Lord Śiva's bow and kill Kaṁsa. Kṛṣṇa felt more at home here than in the city's palaces, and at night He was preoccupied with thoughts of separation from Nanda and His Vṛndāvana friends. Tradition mentions Devī-khara, the nearby grove named after the donkeys that grazed around a temple of Durgā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Balarāma-kuṇḍa
summary: Balarāma-kuṇḍa lies by Dhenukāsura's killing place in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, where brāhmaṇas worship a Deity of Lord Balarāma on its bank.
body: Balarāma-kuṇḍa lies by Dhenukāsura's killing place in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, where brāhmaṇas worship a Deity of Lord Balarāma on its bank. The gopas played here while staying at the kuṇḍa, and Lord Nityānanda stayed here while visiting Mathurā. In the Yoga-pīṭha portrait, Saṅkarṣaṇa-Balarāma resides with His wife Revatī on the southern petal of Vraja in an enchanting grove marked by this kuṇḍa. The kuṇḍa is dried out and visible only during the rainy season.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Balarāma-tīrtha
summary: Balarāma-tīrtha marks the spot where the gopas played while staying at Balarāma-kuṇḍa.
body: Balarāma-tīrtha marks the spot where the gopas played while staying at Balarāma-kuṇḍa. Lord Nityānanda stayed there while visiting Mathurā, and local residents concluded from His ecstasy that He was Daujī Himself. Seeing and praying at this place makes all unhappiness vanish.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Belvana
summary: Belvana is the same forest as Bilvavana and Śrīvana, and it lies at the edge of Māna-sarovara on the eighth forest of Vraja.
body: Belvana is the same forest as Bilvavana and Śrīvana, and it lies at the edge of Māna-sarovara on the eighth forest of Vraja. Its name comes from the bilva, or bel, rose-apple trees growing there, and from the goddess of fortune, Śrī, who still performs austerities here to attain love like that of the gopīs. Caitanya Mahāprabhu visited this forest and recalled while resting here how Kṛṣṇa and the cowherd boys had played. Tradition says that bathing in Māna-sarovara with pure motives transforms a person into a gopī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Beḍokhora-kuñja
summary: Beḍokhora-kuñja is a garden surrounding the samādhi of Kavirāja Gosvāmī and is rich with the pastimes of the divine couple.
body: Beḍokhora-kuñja is a garden surrounding the samādhi of Kavirāja Gosvāmī and is rich with the pastimes of the divine couple. The first weeping willow planted in New Vraja-dhāma marks its inner chamber, and its doors are kept closed by Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, so only They and Their closest devotees know the pastimes there. The lake here is called Kuntala-kuṇḍa, since its waters served the hair of both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Śyāmānanda Paṇḍita's Tilaka-sthāna and puṣpa-samādhi, the ladies' āśrama in New Vraja-dhāma, lie just north.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhadra-sarovara
summary: Bhadra-sarovara is the lake on whose bank Rūpa Gosvāmī completed his drama Lalita-mādhava.
body: Bhadra-sarovara is the lake on whose bank Rūpa Gosvāmī completed his drama Lalita-mādhava. Rūpa Gosvāmī had begun the drama years earlier under the direction of Queen Satyabhāmā, and he developed it further in Purī with Lord Caitanya. Bhadravana, the forest named after Balarāma, is where this completion took place and that even a casual visit there assures one residence in Nāgaloka or the heavenly planets.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhadrakālī-tīrtha
summary: Bhadrakālī-tīrtha lies on the northwest petal of the Yoga-pīṭha, and a kadamba tree there is a meeting place of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, where a hair of Satī is said to have fallen.
body: Bhadrakālī-tīrtha lies on the northwest petal of the Yoga-pīṭha, and a kadamba tree there is a meeting place of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, where a hair of Satī is said to have fallen. Some gopīs worship Kātyāyanī here to get Kṛṣṇa as their husband, and a temple of Kālī called Kātyāyanī-pīṭha stands in the northern corner of Gahvaravana. Rūpa Gosvāmī relates that Lalitā and Viśākhā arranged a full-moon meeting here between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, which Mukharā's arrival interrupted until Kṛṣṇa hid in the bushes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhadāyara-grāma
summary: Bhadāyara-grāma is a village on the hill beyond Rāl, and it is the residence of the gopī Bhadrā, a close friend of Candrāvalī.
body: Bhadāyara-grāma is a village on the hill beyond Rāl, and it is the residence of the gopī Bhadrā, a close friend of Candrāvalī. Bhadrā is named for her auspiciousness and supports Candrāvalī's efforts to monopolise Kṛṣṇa's affections. Unlike Śyāmalā, she is antagonistic to Śrī Rādhā. Tradition notes that prayers are offered to Balarāma while passing Rāl.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhauma-Vṛndāvana
summary: Bhauma-Vṛndāvana is Kṛṣṇa's abode on earth, which He brings with Him from Goloka Vṛndāvana each time He periodically appears.
body: Bhauma-Vṛndāvana is Kṛṣṇa's abode on earth, which He brings with Him from Goloka Vṛndāvana each time He periodically appears. When the Lord returns to Goloka, the place becomes unmanifest, and it is the prototype of New Vraja-dhāma. The parikrama of Kṛṣṇa Valley with a description of Goloka Vṛndāvana, the original of Bhauma Vṛndāvana.

title: Bhegrāma
summary: Bhegrāma is the village where Vajra established Bhāya-grāma, and it is where Jīva Gosvāmī's cave is still found.
body: Bhegrāma is the village where Vajra established Bhāya-grāma, and it is where Jīva Gosvāmī's cave is still found. Rūpa Gosvāmī brought Jīva Gosvāmī back to Vṛndāvana after he had violated a sādhu's duty to be merciful to all, nursed him back to health, and entrusted him with editing his works. At Nanda-ghāṭa there is a temple of Nanda, Yaśodā, and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Downstream is the forest of Vatsavana, which is connected to the killings of Vatsāsura and Aghāsura and to Brahmā's bewilderment.

title: Bhramara-ghāṭa
summary: Bhramara-ghāṭa is a Yamunā ghāṭa that can be seen with Kāliya-ghāṭa from the Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa hill, which is named after the lake in its garden.
body: Bhramara-ghāṭa is a Yamunā ghāṭa that can be seen with Kāliya-ghāṭa from the Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa hill, which is named after the lake in its garden. He once sat by Rāma-kuṇḍa's pavilion and surveyed the length of the Yamunā from Kāliya-ghāṭa to Bhramara-ghāṭa. Tradition says that landmarks at Bhramara-ghāṭa have been installed, and the bank between Cīra-ghāṭa and Bhramara-ghāṭa projects into the river to emphasise Kṛṣṇa's pastimes there.

title: Bhāgavatavana
summary: Bhāgavatavana is a forest in New Vraja-dhāma named after the recitation of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, because both Śukratal and Naimiṣāraṇya mark the spot where Sūta Gosvāmī recited it to sixty thousand sages led by Śaunaka Ṛṣi.
body: Bhāgavatavana is a forest in New Vraja-dhāma named after the recitation of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, because both Śukratal and Naimiṣāraṇya mark the spot where Sūta Gosvāmī recited it to sixty thousand sages led by Śaunaka Ṛṣi. Naimiṣāraṇya is an ancient sacred forest on the bank of the Gomatī River in Uttar Pradesh, and tradition says it is older than Kṛṣṇa's appearance. The forest was named Bhāgavatavana because it combines both places in one forest.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhānu-kuṇḍa
summary: Bhānu-kuṇḍa is the lake in Varṣāṇā where King Vṛṣabhānu found the infant Rādhārāṇī playing within a lotus in a previous day of Brahmā.
body: Bhānu-kuṇḍa is the lake in Varṣāṇā where King Vṛṣabhānu found the infant Rādhārāṇī playing within a lotus in a previous day of Brahmā. In Kṛṣṇa's most recent advent, Rādhā appeared in Rāval, and King Vṛṣabhānu moved his followers from Rāval to Vasatī and then to Varṣāṇā. A deity of Vrajeśvara Mahādeva stands on the bank of the lake. It is called the kuṇḍa the liquid form of King Vṛṣabhānu's love for his daughter.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhānu-sarovara
summary: Bhānu-sarovara, also called Vṛṣabhānu-kuṇḍa, lies on the eastern border of Varṣāṇā, and Mahārāja Vṛṣabhānu bathes there each morning.
body: Bhānu-sarovara, also called Vṛṣabhānu-kuṇḍa, lies on the eastern border of Varṣāṇā, and Mahārāja Vṛṣabhānu bathes there each morning. Some authorities say Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī appeared in Rāval, while others say She appeared from a lotus in this lake, and tradition holds that both views are correct. Rādhā and Her gopī friends bathe on one side of the lake while Kṛṣṇa and His friends bathe on the other, and when only Rādhā and the gopīs are present Kṛṣṇa appears, and the divine couple play water games such as hide-and-seek among the lotuses. The Deities of Laṛilī-Lāl, first established by Vajranābha, once took shelter in the lake's waters when they were under threat.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhāya-grāma
summary: Bhāya-grāma was established by Vajra and is now called Bhegrāma.
body: Bhāya-grāma was established by Vajra and is now called Bhegrāma. Jīva Gosvāmī's cave is still here, and at Nanda-ghāṭa nearby stands a temple of Nanda, Yaśodā and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Devotional accounts recount how Rūpa Gosvāmī, after first banning Jīva Gosvāmī, brought him back to Vṛndāvana, nursed him to health and entrusted him with editing his works such as Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu. Downstream lies the forest of Vatsavana, with places such as Unāi connected to the killing of Vatsāsura and Aghāsura and to Brahmā's bewilderment.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhāṇḍīra-vaṭa
summary: Bhāṇḍīra-vaṭa is a great banyan tree where the cowherd boys rest in the shade and eat their lunches, and where Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and their friends stage dances and other entertainments.
body: Bhāṇḍīra-vaṭa is a great banyan tree where the cowherd boys rest in the shade and eat their lunches, and where Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma and their friends stage dances and other entertainments. It is described as an eternal associate of Kṛṣṇa from Goloka Vṛndāvana who has appeared on earth to serve His pastimes. Kṛṣṇa once came to this tree alone and played a flute melody composed to attract Śrī Rādhā's heart, and He is also said to have wrestled with Rādhā and the gopīs beneath its boughs. Brahmā performed the wedding of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa beneath a banyan of this name, which the account distinguishes from a second Bhāṇḍīra-vaṭa across the Yamunā where Pralambāsura was killed.

title: Bhīṣma-kuṇḍa
summary: Bhīṣma-kuṇḍa, also called Bāṇa-gaṅgā, is a place in the Kurukṣetra area where the grandsire Bhīṣma fell on the tenth day of the battle.
body: Bhīṣma-kuṇḍa, also called Bāṇa-gaṅgā, is a place in the Kurukṣetra area where the grandsire Bhīṣma fell on the tenth day of the battle. To quench Bhīṣma's thirst, Arjuna shot an arrow into the earth and invoked the Ganges. Tradition mentions a second Bāṇa-gaṅgā, where Arjuna created a lake of Ganges water for his horses during the fighting against the Kauravas.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhūlanvana
summary: Bhūlanvana is a dense forest south of Koṭaravana, and its name is explained in two ways, either because many people lose their way there or because Kṛṣṇa warned His friend Subala not to forget (bhulāno) his promise to arrange a meeting with Rādhā.
body: Bhūlanvana is a dense forest south of Koṭaravana, and its name is explained in two ways, either because many people lose their way there or because Kṛṣṇa warned His friend Subala not to forget (bhulāno) his promise to arrange a meeting with Rādhā. Beneath a large bakula tree in the forest is Karamaṇa, where Kṛṣṇa searched for Rādhā late one evening, and in His separation He fainted on a bed of moss and did not meet Her that night. Tradition says the Pāṇḍavas lived incognito at Hoḍal, at the southern edge of the forest, during their last year of exile.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bhūṣaṇavana
summary: Bhūṣaṇavana is a forest in New Vraja-dhāma, opposite Tapovana on the Yamunā, and its name comes from the gopas ornamenting Kṛṣṇa there with fresh sprouts, leaves and flowers.
body: Bhūṣaṇavana is a forest in New Vraja-dhāma, opposite Tapovana on the Yamunā, and its name comes from the gopas ornamenting Kṛṣṇa there with fresh sprouts, leaves and flowers. The cowherd boys concluded that Kṛṣṇa is the ornament of all ornaments, and then walked with Him back to Nandagrāma. In 1994 the Hungarian yātrā first held its summer festivals here in a makeshift temple.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bihārīvana
summary: Bihārīvana is a forest in New Vraja-dhāma that stretches along the road and encompasses Veṇu-kūpa, the samādhi of Madhu Paṇḍita, and the temple of Rādhā-Gopīnātha with its well.
body: Bihārīvana is a forest in New Vraja-dhāma that stretches along the road and encompasses Veṇu-kūpa, the samādhi of Madhu Paṇḍita, and the temple of Rādhā-Gopīnātha with its well. The open field east of the Bāṅke-bihārī temple, called Gopakṛta, was a playground where Kṛṣṇa and the cowherd boys enjoyed their games, and the whole area from there to the samādhi of Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī is counted as Bihārīvana. It is described as home to a playground for Śyāma, a temple for His service, and the final resting places of ācāryas. Tradition mentions that the gopīs avoided the main road and walked a secluded path past this forest with Kṛṣṇa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bodhi-tīrtha
summary: Bodhi-tīrtha is the last of the twenty-four holy places on the Yamunā's bank above and below Viśrāma-ghāṭa on the Mathurā parikrama, and it is said to be equal to Bodhgayā, where Lord Buddha attained perfection.
body: Bodhi-tīrtha is the last of the twenty-four holy places on the Yamunā's bank above and below Viśrāma-ghāṭa on the Mathurā parikrama, and it is said to be equal to Bodhgayā, where Lord Buddha attained perfection. In Tretā-yuga the demon Rāvaṇa came to Vraja and performed austerities on a hill called Rāvaṇa-ṭīlā near this place, seeking to conquer the three worlds. Pilgrims traditionally hear and remember Kṛṣṇa's Mathurā pastimes in the order the places appear on the parikrama path.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Brahma-sarovara
summary: Brahma-sarovara is a lake in Kurukṣetra where Lord Brahmā is said to have created the earth while seated at its centre.
body: Brahma-sarovara is a lake in Kurukṣetra where Lord Brahmā is said to have created the earth while seated at its centre. The Vraja-vāsīs came to Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse to meet Kṛṣṇa and bathed in this lake, and tradition says the gopīs and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī shared affection there with Kṛṣṇa at the centre of the pilgrimage. King Kuru excavated and beautified the area for pilgrims, and tradition says a bath here is equal to one thousand horse sacrifices. Nearby, in the wooded area called Sthāneśvara, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna set up their tents during the war.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Brahma-tīrtha
summary: Brahma-tīrtha is a riverside ghāṭa on the Mathurā parikrama, named after the creator Brahmā, who performed austerities here for one thousand years.
body: Brahma-tīrtha is a riverside ghāṭa on the Mathurā parikrama, named after the creator Brahmā, who performed austerities here for one thousand years. He still guides pilgrims here to Viṣṇuloka. The next ghāṭa is Ghaṇṭābharaṇa-ghāṭa, where bathing is said to lead to the planet of the sun god. Tradition also assigns Brahma-tīrtha to the cheerfulness of Govardhana Hill in its description of the hill as a living form.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Brahmavana
summary: Brahmavana appears in devotional accounts's listing of the sub-forests (upavanas) of Vraja, where it is identified with Brahma-kuṇḍa.
body: Brahmavana appears in devotional accounts's listing of the sub-forests (upavanas) of Vraja, where it is identified with Brahma-kuṇḍa. It is mentioned mainly in passing, as part of a catalogue of forests and their locations rather than through any pastime. The opulences of Vṛndāvana can be reproduced in New Vraja-dhāma as Kṛṣṇa wills.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Bṛhadvana
summary: Bṛhadvana is another name for Mahāvana, the twelfth forest of Vraja.
body: Bṛhadvana is another name for Mahāvana, the twelfth forest of Vraja. Nanda Mahārāja was attached to living there, but for the sake of his subjects, who were unhappy, he agreed to move the cowherd community to Vṛndāvana. Tradition says that Mahārāja Parjanya moved his dependents to Mahāvana, where it offered safety and abundant grass for the cows. The forest is described as the object of meditation for devotees who aspire for love of God, and it is said that fasting, bathing and worshipping there frees one from sin.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Cakra-tīrtha
summary: Cakra-tīrtha is a ghāṭa on the Mathurā riverfront beside Ambarīṣa-ṭīlā, where Kṛṣṇa's disc, which He gave to King Ambarīṣa, is said to reside.
body: Cakra-tīrtha is a ghāṭa on the Mathurā riverfront beside Ambarīṣa-ṭīlā, where Kṛṣṇa's disc, which He gave to King Ambarīṣa, is said to reside. Uddhava met Kṛṣṇa near this place beneath a banyan tree by the Yamunā, having promised to bring Kṛṣṇa back home to Vraja. Sanātana Gosvāmī lived here, worshipping Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in a cottage facing Lord Śiva, and he left his body here. Śiva, known here as Cakreśvara, persuaded the mosquito demigod to clear the area so Sanātana would stay.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Campakalatānandada-kuñja
summary: Campakalatānandada-kuñja is the golden grove on the south side of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, opposite Lalitā's grove.
body: Campakalatānandada-kuñja is the golden grove on the south side of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, opposite Lalitā's grove. Everything in it is golden, either by nature or by reflection from the golden ground, and the grove is dense with golden vines and trees. Rādhā, who is golden-complexioned, comes to this grove, and the account describes it as one of the sakhī groves around the kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Candanavana
summary: Candanavana is a forest of sandalwood trees adjoining Nandavana, beyond which lie open pastures and the lake Loṭana-kuṇḍa with its sandy banks.
body: Candanavana is a forest of sandalwood trees adjoining Nandavana, beyond which lie open pastures and the lake Loṭana-kuṇḍa with its sandy banks. The name of the lake comes from the cows rolling (loṭ) in the cool sand on a hot day while the gopas watched. Kṛṣṇa used to graze His herd here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Candrāvalī-kuṇḍa
summary: Candrāvalī-kuṇḍa is a lake in a forest near Rīṭhorā, the village of the gopa Candrabhānu and the birthplace of Candrāvalī.
body: Candrāvalī-kuṇḍa is a lake in a forest near Rīṭhorā, the village of the gopa Candrabhānu and the birthplace of Candrāvalī. As a young girl, Candrāvalī and her friends played and bathed in its waters and rested under a kadamba tree on its bank. Followers of Rūpa Gosvāmī see Candrāvalī as an expansion of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's personal form, displaying her submissive aspect.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Cayana-ghāṭa
summary: Cayana-ghāṭa, also known as Cīra-ghāṭa, is a place in New Vraja-dhāma where the Yamunā's bank projects into the water between Cīra-ghāṭa and Bhramara-ghāṭa, giving emphasis to the pastimes Kṛṣṇa enjoys there.
body: Cayana-ghāṭa, also known as Cīra-ghāṭa, is a place in New Vraja-dhāma where the Yamunā's bank projects into the water between Cīra-ghāṭa and Bhramara-ghāṭa, giving emphasis to the pastimes Kṛṣṇa enjoys there. It is often confused with another Cīra-ghāṭa in Tapovana, where the Vraja-kumārīs worshipped goddess Kātyāyanī. The two should be distinguished.

title: Cena-ghāṭa
summary: Cena-ghāṭa is the original name of Cīra-ghāṭa, according to Jīva Gosvāmī, derived from cena, meaning the happiness of resting, in the Mathurā dialect.
body: Cena-ghāṭa is the original name of Cīra-ghāṭa, according to Jīva Gosvāmī, derived from cena, meaning the happiness of resting, in the Mathurā dialect. After Kṛṣṇa killed the demon Keśī at Keśī-tīrtha, the weary crowd went to rest here, and while they rested Kṛṣṇa walked along the Yamunā. Nārada Muni met Kṛṣṇa in a secluded place at that time and begged Him to relieve the sufferings of Mathurā's residents.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Chatravana
summary: Chatravana is a forest where Rādhā worships the sun god at Sūrya-kuṇḍa, which lies between Dabharāro and Cikṣolī, and tradition notes that sun-named lakes are found at various places in Vraja.
body: Chatravana is a forest where Rādhā worships the sun god at Sūrya-kuṇḍa, which lies between Dabharāro and Cikṣolī, and tradition notes that sun-named lakes are found at various places in Vraja. North of Dabharāro is Muktā-kuṇḍa, also called Ratna-kuṇḍa, whose glories are described in the work Muktā-carita. The name Dabharāro comes from a pastime in which Kṛṣṇa's eyes flooded (ḍubu) with tears, after which the locals named their village that. Tradition mentions that a deity of Siddha-Hanumān is taken in procession from Khoṅha to Chātā, which is Chatravana, on Hanumān-jayantī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Chattravana
summary: Chattravana is the forest where the gopas crowned Kṛṣṇa, and where Rādhā's coronation was performed twice, first as play by the gopīs and then with full pomp by the Vraja-vāsīs.
body: Chattravana is the forest where the gopas crowned Kṛṣṇa, and where Rādhā's coronation was performed twice, first as play by the gopīs and then with full pomp by the Vraja-vāsīs. These events were part of a greater pastime arranged by Yogamāyā to establish Rādhā's sovereignty over Kṛṣṇa, Vraja and the Vraja-vāsīs. Devotional accounts describe Madhumaṅgala being bound by the gopī guards and returning to Kṛṣṇa at Chattravana, and the account says the gopas rested at Biḍāvala while negotiations took place. The temple of Rādhā-vallabha stands in the northeastern corner of the forest.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Chācha-kuṇḍa
summary: Chācha-kuṇḍa lies on the edge of Domīlavana forest, where the excess buttermilk (chācha) of the Vraja-vāsīs is either discarded by their servants or consumed by the cowherd boys.
body: Chācha-kuṇḍa lies on the edge of Domīlavana forest, where the excess buttermilk (chācha) of the Vraja-vāsīs is either discarded by their servants or consumed by the cowherd boys. It is near the lovely Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa, where Uddhava bathed on his first morning in Vraja and from where he saw the gopīs gathered around his chariot. Tradition mentions Pānīhārī-kuṇḍa nearby, where Rādhārāṇī and Mother Rohiṇī cook in summer.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Cintāharaṇa-ghāṭa
summary: Cintāharaṇa-ghāṭa is near Brahmāṇḍa-ghāṭa and is named after the anxiety (cintā) Mother Yaśodā felt when she saw the universal form in her son's mouth.
body: Cintāharaṇa-ghāṭa is near Brahmāṇḍa-ghāṭa and is named after the anxiety (cintā) Mother Yaśodā felt when she saw the universal form in her son's mouth. A deity of Lord Śiva is worshipped here, because Yaśodā prayed to him to free (haraṇa) Kṛṣṇa from that dangerous situation, and he relieved her anxiety. Tradition also places it at the lower segment of the Golden Yamunā, which runs from Rāval to Cintāharaṇa-ghāṭa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Cintāmaṇi-dhāma
summary: Cintāmaṇi-dhāma is mentioned in mainly in passing, in a passage about how Vraja transforms curses into blessings.
body: Cintāmaṇi-dhāma is mentioned in mainly in passing, in a passage about how Vraja transforms curses into blessings. A traditional verse quotes Jīva Gosvāmī saying that in Vṛndāvana even the inexpert efforts of poets will be hailed as poetry. Devotional accounts give no pastime connected with the place itself.

title: Citrānandada-kuñja
summary: Citrānandada-kuñja is the grove of Citrā-devī on the eastern shore of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and it is called it the embodiment of diversity and wonder.
body: Citrānandada-kuñja is the grove of Citrā-devī on the eastern shore of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and it is called it the embodiment of diversity and wonder. It is swarming with birds and bees and is more colourful than Viśākhā's kuñja, with trees, vines, jewels, platforms, swings and pavilions in every hue. Its name means the grove that gives bliss (ānanda) to Citrā, following the same naming pattern as the other sakhī groves.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Cyavana
summary: Cyavana is mentioned in devotional accounts mainly in passing, as the sage who married the daughter of Mahārāja Śaryāti.
body: Cyavana is mentioned in devotional accounts mainly in passing, as the sage who married the daughter of Mahārāja Śaryāti. The footnote in which he appears recounts the story of King Kakudmī's daughter Revatī and her marriage to Lord Balarāma, as found in Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and Garga-saṁhitā. No pastime is described at Cyavana's own place.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Cāmelivana
summary: Cāmelivana is a forest just south of Bhūlanvana, and some say the two are one forest while others say they are separate.
body: Cāmelivana is a forest just south of Bhūlanvana, and some say the two are one forest while others say they are separate. It is named for the abundance of cāmeli trees whose fragrance perfumes the area, and the account describes it as a place where wonderful pastimes of the divine couple occur. Asks why Kṛṣṇa wanders in forests like Cāmelivana, and answers, quoting Śrīla Prabhupāda, that He does so to please the gopīs, the cowherd boys, the birds, the bees and the cows.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dadhi-grāma
summary: Dadhi-grāma is a village in a corner of Koṭaravana, where Kṛṣṇa stole yogurt (dadhi) from the gopīs to bring them pleasure and to feed His friends.
body: Dadhi-grāma is a village in a corner of Koṭaravana, where Kṛṣṇa stole yogurt (dadhi) from the gopīs to bring them pleasure and to feed His friends. The gopīs offered yogurt daily to a deity of goddess Pārvatī worshipped on a mound beside a lake, so she was known as Dadhi-devī and the lake as Dadhi-kuṇḍa. Tradition says that the cowherd boys, while on a search for milk, were given milk at the village now called Paya-grāma.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dadhi-kuṇḍa
summary: Dadhi-kuṇḍa is a lake beside the mound where the goddess Pārvatī is worshipped as Dadhi-devī.
body: Dadhi-kuṇḍa is a lake beside the mound where the goddess Pārvatī is worshipped as Dadhi-devī. One day Kṛṣṇa and the gopas blocked the gopīs on their way with offerings of yogurt and claimed it, telling them that Pārvatī, Sarasvatī and Kālī are His maidservants. He then distributed the yogurt before the goddess, and the gopīs saw her lips seem to smile as they looked at her.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dadhi-manthana-sthala
summary: Dadhi-manthana-sthala is the veranda of Mahārāja Nanda's palace, where Mother Yaśodā churned yogurt and Kṛṣṇa angrily broke the churn.
body: Dadhi-manthana-sthala is the veranda of Mahārāja Nanda's palace, where Mother Yaśodā churned yogurt and Kṛṣṇa angrily broke the churn. Yaśodā caught and tied Kṛṣṇa in the courtyard below, and He uprooted the twin arjuna trees at Yamalārjuna-bhañjana-tīrtha near the Yamunā. Since this pastime Kṛṣṇa has been known by the name Dāmodara, which comes from the silk ribbon Yaśodā used to bind Him.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dadhīci-kuṇḍa
summary: Dadhīci-kuṇḍa is the lake where the sage Dadhīci performed austerities and gave up his body at Indra's request, and from his bones Viśvakarmā created the thunderbolt with which Indra defeated Vṛtra.
body: Dadhīci-kuṇḍa is the lake where the sage Dadhīci performed austerities and gave up his body at Indra's request, and from his bones Viśvakarmā created the thunderbolt with which Indra defeated Vṛtra. Those who bathe here awaken the sage's spirit of selfless service and detachment from the body. A self-manifest deity of ten-cubit Hanumān, carrying Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa on his shoulders, stands at the kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Daharavana
summary: Daharavana is a forest to the north of Abhimanyu's mansion in Yāvaṭā.
body: Daharavana is a forest to the north of Abhimanyu's mansion in Yāvaṭā. When Kṛṣṇa could not enter the bolted gate, He climbed a berī tree at the edge of Daharavana near Rādhā's windows and called to Her with a cuckoo-like voice while Jaṭilā slept. Tradition describes Abhimanyu, Rādhā's husband, whose mansion is a kind of prison to her, and says he is a friend of Govardhana Malla, the husband of Candrāvalī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Danta-dhāvana
summary: Danta-dhāvana is a small hill (ṭīlā) south of Mahārāja Nanda's palace where the king brushed his teeth (danta-dhāvana) each morning.
body: Danta-dhāvana is a small hill (ṭīlā) south of Mahārāja Nanda's palace where the king brushed his teeth (danta-dhāvana) each morning. Nearby, in the palace courtyard, stood a makeshift wrestling arena where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma wrestled with each other, while elderly gopīs came to tempt the brothers to play. Kṛṣṇa killed the demon Śakaṭāsura by overturning a cart not far from this arena.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭa
summary: Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭa is a ghāṭa in Mathurā where an elaborate horse sacrifice was performed on the banks of the Yamunā for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure, and a bath here is said to yield the fruit of ten such sacrifices.
body: Daśāśvamedha-ghāṭa is a ghāṭa in Mathurā where an elaborate horse sacrifice was performed on the banks of the Yamunā for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure, and a bath here is said to yield the fruit of ten such sacrifices. Next to it is Ambarīṣa-ṭīlā, where King Ambarīṣa observed the Dvādaśī vow, and then Cakra-tīrtha. Tradition recounts that Uddhava's house lay on the way to this ghāṭa, and after Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were crowned with Ugrasena's coronation, Uddhava met them and lost awareness of time in their company. Rūpa Gosvāmī received instruction from Caitanya Mahāprabhu here before going on to Vṛndāvana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Daśāśvamedha-tīrtha
summary: Daśāśvamedha-tīrtha lies further downstream from Gokarṇa-ghāṭa and is always worshipped by great sages, and self-controlled persons bathe here to easily attain the pleasures of the heavenly planets.
body: Daśāśvamedha-tīrtha lies further downstream from Gokarṇa-ghāṭa and is always worshipped by great sages, and self-controlled persons bathe here to easily attain the pleasures of the heavenly planets. In days of yore an elaborate horse sacrifice was performed on the Yamunā's banks for Kṛṣṇa's pleasure, and a bath at this ghāṭa yields the fruit of ten such sacrifices.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Daṇḍi-ghāṭa
summary: Daṇḍi-ghāṭa is a bathing place adjoining Tinduka-tīrtha, named after Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who bathed here as a daṇḍī (sannyāsī), and it is also called Bengali-ghāṭa.
body: Daṇḍi-ghāṭa is a bathing place adjoining Tinduka-tīrtha, named after Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who bathed here as a daṇḍī (sannyāsī), and it is also called Bengali-ghāṭa. Devotional accounts describe nearby Tinduka-tīrtha, where a destitute barber named Tinduka bathed regularly and was reborn as an aristocratic brāhmaṇa after death. Next is Sūrya-tīrtha, where Bali Mahārāja pleased the sun god and received a cintāmaṇi gem.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Deha-kuṇḍa
summary: Deha-kuṇḍa is a confidential pastime place on the far side of Ūñchagaon, where the gopīs unconditionally gave themselves body (deha) and soul to Kṛṣṇa.
body: Deha-kuṇḍa is a confidential pastime place on the far side of Ūñchagaon, where the gopīs unconditionally gave themselves body (deha) and soul to Kṛṣṇa. Devotional accounts recount how, while a marriage festival was going on nearby, a poor brāhmaṇa approached the sporting gopīs and Kṛṣṇa and asked for material wealth, after which the gopīs installed a deity of Mahādeva called Veṇīśaṅkara on the lake's banks. Bathing here and seeing Lord Śiva surpasses bathing at the Prayāga confluence.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Devaśīrṣa-kuṇḍa
summary: Devaśīrṣa-kuṇḍa is in Kāmyavana, where the demigods offered exalted (śīrṣa) prayers to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, and the flowers the demigods and their wives showered upon the brothers became this lake.
body: Devaśīrṣa-kuṇḍa is in Kāmyavana, where the demigods offered exalted (śīrṣa) prayers to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, and the flowers the demigods and their wives showered upon the brothers became this lake. The demigods still identified with their universal posts and could not approach the Lord, but some sages who gave up false designations reached the topmost perfection at nearby Muniśīrṣa-sthāna.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Devī-dhāma
summary: Devī-dhāma is the mundane world, the lowest of the realms in a verse from Brahma-saṁhitā quoted in devotional literature, above which lie Maheśa-dhāma and Hari-dhāma, and highest of all is Kṛṣṇa's own realm, Goloka.
body: Devī-dhāma is the mundane world, the lowest of the realms in a verse from Brahma-saṁhitā quoted in devotional literature, above which lie Maheśa-dhāma and Hari-dhāma, and highest of all is Kṛṣṇa's own realm, Goloka. This verse glorifies Goloka Vṛndāvana as superior to all the Lord's other abodes. Tradition says that Vṛṣabhānu-pura, Varṣāṇā, is untouched by Hari-dhāma or Devī-dhāma, because it is permeated by Rādhā's sweet youthfulness.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhanus-tīrtha
summary: Dhanus-tīrtha is the place of the sacrificial bow in Kṛṣṇa Valley, the open area in Mathurā flanked by two life-size resin elephants, and it lies beside Raṅga-bhūmi, the wrestling arena.
body: Dhanus-tīrtha is the place of the sacrificial bow in Kṛṣṇa Valley, the open area in Mathurā flanked by two life-size resin elephants, and it lies beside Raṅga-bhūmi, the wrestling arena. Kṛṣṇa broke the bow here, and nearby Kaṁsa-ṭīlā marks where Kaṁsa was slain. Raṅgeśvara Mahādeva, whom Kaṁsa installed in the hope of defeating Kṛṣṇa, protects this corner of Mathurā, and the wrestling tournament took place on Śiva-rātri.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dharma-kuṇḍa
summary: Dharma-kuṇḍa is a secluded lake in Kāmyavana, full of lotuses and lilies, where the Pāṇḍavas came while thirsty during their stay in Kāman.
body: Dharma-kuṇḍa is a secluded lake in Kāmyavana, full of lotuses and lilies, where the Pāṇḍavas came while thirsty during their stay in Kāman. While they chased a deer that had run off with a brāhmaṇa's ladle and araṇi sticks, Nakula went to fetch water and died after ignoring a celestial warning, and Sahadeva, Arjuna and Bhīma each went to the lake and died in the same way. The parikrama of Kāmyavana traditionally begins with a bath at Dharma-kuṇḍa or Vimala-kuṇḍa, and pilgrims often visit Dharma-kuṇḍa inside Kāman.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhoyāni-kuṇḍa
summary: A small lake near the main road to Varṣāṇā, where Mother Yaśodā's servants washed the yogurt pots while singing of Kṛṣṇa.
body: A small lake near the main road to Varṣāṇā, where Mother Yaśodā's servants washed the yogurt pots while singing of Kṛṣṇa. Devotional accounts describe Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa at its ghāṭa, glancing at each other as they absentmindedly dipped their pots, so enchanted by each other's youthful beauty that they dropped the pots or forgot to pull them out until the gopīs' laughter woke them. It stands beside Pānīhārī-kuṇḍa and across from Sārasika-yuḍi on the road to Nandagrāma.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhruva-ghāṭa
summary: This is one of the twenty-four bathing ghāṭas of Mathurā, ninth in Śrīla Prabhupāda's list.
body: This is one of the twenty-four bathing ghāṭas of Mathurā, ninth in Śrīla Prabhupāda's list. Rūpa Gosvāmī, sent by Lord Caitanya to Vṛndāvana in 1517, lived here until Sanātana Gosvāmī joined him. In 1519 the two brothers met at Dhruva-ghāṭa and realised their long-cherished dream of living together in Vṛndāvana, after which Rūpa settled in Sevā-kuñja and Sanātana lived atop Dvādaśāditya-ṭīlā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhruva-tīrtha
summary: Downstream from Vaṭasvāmī-tīrtha, this is where child Dhruva performed severe austerities for four months, standing on one leg and concentrating fully on the Lord, and the pressure of his big toe left footprints that are still visible.
body: Downstream from Vaṭasvāmī-tīrtha, this is where child Dhruva performed severe austerities for four months, standing on one leg and concentrating fully on the Lord, and the pressure of his big toe left footprints that are still visible. Devotees who want unwavering determination in devotional service bathe and worship here. Overlooking it is Nārada-ṭīlā, from which Nārada Muni watched Dhruva's obstinate determination, and nearby Saptarṣi-ghāṭa is the place where the seven sages are associated with the site.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhyāna-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake marks the spot where Kṛṣṇa sat in meditation (dhyāna) on Rādhā, remembering Her features, Her witty talks, and their recent dancing and enjoyment in the groves.
body: This lake marks the spot where Kṛṣṇa sat in meditation (dhyāna) on Rādhā, remembering Her features, Her witty talks, and their recent dancing and enjoyment in the groves. Because His thoughts of Rādhā are not different from Her, they formed a pathway to Her lotus feet, and the lake where that pathway began is called Dhyāna-kuṇḍa. It is linked to Caraṇa-pahāṛī and the nearby Vihvala-kuṇḍa, where Kṛṣṇa's flute music bewildered Rādhā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhārāpatana-tīrtha
summary: Located at the foot of Kaṁsa-ṭīlā, part of the fortification around Mathurā, its waters are said to assure heavenly happiness or, if desired, eternal life in Vaikuṇṭha.
body: Located at the foot of Kaṁsa-ṭīlā, part of the fortification around Mathurā, its waters are said to assure heavenly happiness or, if desired, eternal life in Vaikuṇṭha. The immortal snake Ananta, who protects the dhāma from here, appeared to shelter Vasudeva and baby Kṛṣṇa from wind and rain on their way to Gokula. Tradition tells of a king and queen who, after the queen's previous life of drowning here, bathed at the next tīrtha, Saṁyamana-tīrtha, and went to Goloka.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dhīra-samīra-ghāṭa
summary: On the shore between Keśī-ghāṭa and Vaṁśīvaṭa in New Vraja-dhāma, its gardens and groves represent the place where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa perfected Their youth.
body: On the shore between Keśī-ghāṭa and Vaṁśīvaṭa in New Vraja-dhāma, its gardens and groves represent the place where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa perfected Their youth. In Bhauma Vṛndāvana the gardens have disappeared and the Yamunā no longer flows nearby, yet the breezes (samīra) still blow softly (dhīra) there. Jayadeva Gosvāmī described the significance of this part of the Yamunā and of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Dhūlāuda-grāma
summary: This village lies just outside the parikrama path, near Kāmyavana and close to Udhā and Āṭora.
body: This village lies just outside the parikrama path, near Kāmyavana and close to Udhā and Āṭora. Devotional accounts recount how the dust raised by the combined movements of the cows and gopas rose so high that it reached the heavens, blinding the demigods and making them call out in alarm. It contrasts this with the usual grazing in grassy pastures, where little dust is stirred up.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dohanī-kuṇḍa
summary: Dohanī-kuṇḍa lies east of Muktā-kuṇḍa among the holy places west of Varṣāṇā, and the surrounding area is named after it.
body: Dohanī-kuṇḍa lies east of Muktā-kuṇḍa among the holy places west of Varṣāṇā, and the surrounding area is named after it. It is the site of King Vṛṣabhānu's barns and corrals, where he keeps and waters his vast herd of cows and bulls. Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī often comes here with Her girlfriends to watch the cows being milked, and sometimes they milk the cows themselves.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Domanavana
summary: This expansive forest, reached by walking the parikrama path counterclockwise around Nandagrāma, is the same forest as Domīlavana and is also known as Domanavana.
body: This expansive forest, reached by walking the parikrama path counterclockwise around Nandagrāma, is the same forest as Domīlavana and is also known as Domanavana. The name reflects the meeting (milana) of the two lovers Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and the merging of Their minds (mana) in pastimes of youthful love. Two hidden lakes, Runakī-kuṇḍa and Jhunakī-kuṇḍa, are named after two gopīs who arranged the couple's meeting.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Domīlavana
summary: Reached by following the parikrama path counterclockwise around Nandagrāma, this expansive forest is where the two lovers, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, meet, and its name is explained by dvā (two) and milana (meeting).
body: Reached by following the parikrama path counterclockwise around Nandagrāma, this expansive forest is where the two lovers, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, meet, and its name is explained by dvā (two) and milana (meeting). It is also called Domanavana, because the minds (mana) of the divine couple merge here in pastimes of transcendental youthful love. Two hidden lakes, Runakī-kuṇḍa and Jhunakī-kuṇḍa, bear the names of two gopīs who arranged their meeting, and on the forest's edge is Chācha-kuṇḍa, where the surplus buttermilk is discarded or consumed by the cowherd boys.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Droṇa-tīrtha
summary: The cowherd boys named this place when servants Raktaka and Patraka gathered large cup-shaped kadamba leaves to serve as bowls for eating yogurt in the shade of a giant kadamba tree.
body: The cowherd boys named this place when servants Raktaka and Patraka gathered large cup-shaped kadamba leaves to serve as bowls for eating yogurt in the shade of a giant kadamba tree. Ever since, the boys came to the banks of Nīpa-kuṇḍa here to eat their lunches from the leaf-cups. In the description of Govardhana Hill as Kṛṣṇa's form, Droṇa-tīrtha is said to be the hill's back.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dugdha-kuṇḍa
summary: Also called Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa and Kṣīra-sāgara, this lake is where the priests of the Deity Daujī threw Him upside down when soldiers of Muslim kings came to raze the temple.
body: Also called Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa and Kṣīra-sāgara, this lake is where the priests of the Deity Daujī threw Him upside down when soldiers of Muslim kings came to raze the temple. The Deity remained in the lake for many years until cowherd men noticed two cows pouring their milk onto a protruding rock by the lakeside. Daujī was one of the few Deities who never left Vraja for Jaipur, although He had to be hidden at various times to avoid attacks.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Durvāsā-kuṇḍa
summary: One of Durvāsā Muni's Vṛndāvana āśramas stands at this lake, from which the nearby Kāmara can be seen a short distance south.
body: One of Durvāsā Muni's Vṛndāvana āśramas stands at this lake, from which the nearby Kāmara can be seen a short distance south. Devotional accounts describe how, when Kṛṣṇa played His flute, the water in nearby rivers and lakes such as Durvāsā-kuṇḍa turned into a pleasant semi-solid substance, and the rocks on Caraṇa-pahāṛī turned soft like putty. It is mentioned mainly in connection with these events.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dvādaśasūrya-tīrtha
summary: Devotional accounts recount that when Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by the gopas, gopīs and surabhi cows, felt uncomfortable in the winter cold, twelve suns appeared at this place and warmed Him with their intense shining.
body: Devotional accounts recount that when Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by the gopas, gopīs and surabhi cows, felt uncomfortable in the winter cold, twelve suns appeared at this place and warmed Him with their intense shining. The perspiration that fell from His body then became a charming, clear lake, which is why the place bears the name Dvādaśasūrya-tīrtha. The site is honoured through verses of worship and shelter.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Dvādaśāditya-tīrtha
summary: When Rādhā, in despair after Kṛṣṇa's rejection, decided to drown Her body in the waters of Kāliya Lake, She sent word through Viśākhā that She had gone to Dvādaśāditya-tīrtha to worship the sun god.
body: When Rādhā, in despair after Kṛṣṇa's rejection, decided to drown Her body in the waters of Kāliya Lake, She sent word through Viśākhā that She had gone to Dvādaśāditya-tīrtha to worship the sun god. Viśākhā, relieved at the apparent change in Rādhā's attitude, let Her go, and the two set out towards the Yamunā with different plans in mind. Devotional accounts describe this place in the context of Rādhā's sorrow.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Dvārakā-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake lies in the area between Candrasena Hill and Kāman, where Kṛṣṇa brought His wives from Dvārakā, stayed with them in a city of tents, and showed them His footprints.
body: This lake lies in the area between Candrasena Hill and Kāman, where Kṛṣṇa brought His wives from Dvārakā, stayed with them in a city of tents, and showed them His footprints. The nearby marks on the hill, called caraṇa-pahāṛī, to Kṛṣṇa's footprints. It also recounts that after a night of dancing with the gopīs in Kāmyavana, Kṛṣṇa climbed Candrasena Hill to entice His beloved.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dāmodara-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake is mentioned mainly in passing, as one of several lakes in the Kāmyavana area, listed in a note together with Veda-kuṇḍa, Gandharva-kuṇḍa, Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa, Arghya-kuṇḍa and Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa.
body: This lake is mentioned mainly in passing, as one of several lakes in the Kāmyavana area, listed in a note together with Veda-kuṇḍa, Gandharva-kuṇḍa, Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa, Arghya-kuṇḍa and Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa. Little more is said about it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dāmodaravana
summary: This garden forest near the back end of the Rādhā-Dāmodara temple, between Baḍa-baṭhain and Nikuñja-mandira, is landscaped to resemble the descriptions of Vraja's sub-forests.
body: This garden forest near the back end of the Rādhā-Dāmodara temple, between Baḍa-baṭhain and Nikuñja-mandira, is landscaped to resemble the descriptions of Vraja's sub-forests. Its flowers, shade trees and fruit orchards attract birds, bees and devotees seeking a secluded place for nāma-saṅkīrtana. Within it is a rose garden called Gula-camana, with a small lake named Gula-kuṇḍa, created for the pleasure of Rādhā-Dāmodara and Rādhā-Śyāmasundara.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dāna-mandira
summary: This temple stands on the northern part of Dāna-gaṛh, a hill in Varṣāṇā named because it overlooks the place where Kṛṣṇa regularly demands a toll (dāna) from the cowherd girls.
body: This temple stands on the northern part of Dāna-gaṛh, a hill in Varṣāṇā named because it overlooks the place where Kṛṣṇa regularly demands a toll (dāna) from the cowherd girls. In Bhauma Vṛndāvana, an ancient set of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Deities called Rādhā–Dāna-bihārī was installed here six thousand years ago. The presence of these Deities answers the claim of some scholars that worship of Kṛṣṇa with Rādhā began less than five hundred years ago.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Dāna-nivartana-kuṇḍa
summary: This clear lake lies by Govardhana Hill in the forest where Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs enacted the toll pastime, and it takes its name from the gopīs' promise to return (nivartana) to pay the toll (dāna) they owed.
body: This clear lake lies by Govardhana Hill in the forest where Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs enacted the toll pastime, and it takes its name from the gopīs' promise to return (nivartana) to pay the toll (dāna) they owed. Devotional accounts describe the large offerings made in sacrifice on the area from this lake to Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa, and it mentions Kṛṣṇa-vedī, below the hill, where the divine couple enjoyed these pastimes. Near the lake is the ISKCON Bhaktivedanta Āśrama, which affords a view of Girirāja and the pastime places.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dāna-nivartana-vana
summary: This forest surrounds Dāna-nivartana-kuṇḍa, and the account gives a second meaning for the name based on a pastime there.
body: This forest surrounds Dāna-nivartana-kuṇḍa, and the account gives a second meaning for the name based on a pastime there. Kṛṣṇa knelt before Rādhā and said namo 'stu te, and when Lalitā prodded Him with her whip, He placed His head on Her lotus toes, leaving the forest completely silent in wonder. This is remembered as the confidential picture of the Supreme Person bowing to a cowherd maiden.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dāna-sarovara
summary: This is another name for Dāna-nivartana-kuṇḍa, given because Kṛṣṇa enjoyed the dāna-keli pastime with His cowherd friends in a secluded place by its shore.
body: This is another name for Dāna-nivartana-kuṇḍa, given because Kṛṣṇa enjoyed the dāna-keli pastime with His cowherd friends in a secluded place by its shore. The lake's truths remain hidden from those averse to pure devotion, and tradition prays to reside here. The verses quoted describe its cool, fragrant water, which gives transcendental virtues to all who drink it, and the lake is where the divine couple enjoy the dāna-keli pastime.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Dāvānala-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake marks the place where the Vraja-vāsīs were surrounded by the ring of forest fire, and where the fire actually broke out and raged out of control.
body: This lake marks the place where the Vraja-vāsīs were surrounded by the ring of forest fire, and where the fire actually broke out and raged out of control. Nearby stands the temple of Dāvānala-bihārī, where Kṛṣṇa stood as He swallowed the fire. Ṭhākura Bhaktivinoda saw this fire as representing quarrels among Vaiṣṇavas, and suggests that devotees keep some earth from the kuṇḍa as a reminder.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Dṛśyamāna-dhāma
summary: This is not a single physical place but the term for the dhāma after Kṛṣṇa's disappearance, when the unmanifest dhāma is felt through a visible material covering.
body: This is not a single physical place but the term for the dhāma after Kṛṣṇa's disappearance, when the unmanifest dhāma is felt through a visible material covering. While Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet touched the earth, the sweetness and majesty of Goloka were visible in Bhauma Vṛndāvana. After His departure, Kṛṣṇa invokes His antardhāna-śakti, so the aprakaṭa features of the dhāma are obscured from ordinary vision as Kali-yuga progresses.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Ekāmravana
summary: Devotional accounts mention this place in passing, noting that Lord Caitanya, while touring south India, arrived at Ekāmravana in Bhuvaneśvara and met Lord Śiva in person.
body: Devotional accounts mention this place in passing, noting that Lord Caitanya, while touring south India, arrived at Ekāmravana in Bhuvaneśvara and met Lord Śiva in person. A prayer Lord Caitanya recited there is also remembered, offering obeisances to Lord Śiva as the lord of the thirty primal demigods and the original father of created beings.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gahvara-kuṇḍa
summary: Vaiṣṇavas reach this lake along the path through Gahvaravana, and it is called Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa because of the many pastimes Kṛṣṇa enacts on its banks and Śītala-kuṇḍa because its water stays cool even in summer.
body: Vaiṣṇavas reach this lake along the path through Gahvaravana, and it is called Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa because of the many pastimes Kṛṣṇa enacts on its banks and Śītala-kuṇḍa because its water stays cool even in summer. Devotional accounts recount how the boys roasted stolen chickpeas here, and how an old gopī who came to scold them was won over by Kṛṣṇa's beauty and began to feed Him as her own son. It also describes Rādhā waiting anxiously near this lake after Kṛṣṇa had failed to keep their appointment, until a parrot reported that He had been with Candrāvalī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Gajendra-mokṣaṇa-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake lies in the corner of Prabhupādavana and represents the lake in the Raṅgajī temple of Bhauma Vṛndāvana where the deliverance of the elephant Gajendra is enacted every year.
body: This lake lies in the corner of Prabhupādavana and represents the lake in the Raṅgajī temple of Bhauma Vṛndāvana where the deliverance of the elephant Gajendra is enacted every year. Devotional accounts describe how Gajendra was captured by a crocodile while bathing, and how the Lord finally appeared to answer the elephant king's prayer. Tradition then continued on to Brahma-kuṇḍa from here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gandharva-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake lies at the centre of Gandheśvara, where Vṛndāvana's perfume-makers kept flower gardens and made scents from the seasonal blossoms.
body: This lake lies at the centre of Gandheśvara, where Vṛndāvana's perfume-makers kept flower gardens and made scents from the seasonal blossoms. While herding their cows nearby, Kṛṣṇa and the gopas came to Gandheśvara to test the scents, though Kṛṣṇa was interested only in which one would attract Śrī Rādhā. Tradition notes that in Parāsaulī village the Gandharvas marvelled at Kṛṣṇa's divine singing here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gandharva-sakhā-kuñja
summary: Lord Caitanya, accompanied by Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, came to the solitude of this grove, sat beneath a tamāla tree, and remembered the pastimes Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs once enjoyed here.
body: Lord Caitanya, accompanied by Balabhadra Bhaṭṭācārya, came to the solitude of this grove, sat beneath a tamāla tree, and remembered the pastimes Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs once enjoyed here. At Tamāla-talā, as the warm autumn breeze caressed His body, He sometimes sank into the ecstasy of Śrī Rādhā and sometimes remembered that He was Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Before this, tradition notes that He had marked His body with tilaka made from the mud of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gandharvānandada-kuñja
summary: This grove, to the southeast of the grove supervised by Indulekhā, belongs to the gopa Gandharva and displays a dazzling array of colours and forms.
body: This grove, to the southeast of the grove supervised by Indulekhā, belongs to the gopa Gandharva and displays a dazzling array of colours and forms. Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs enjoy swing pastimes here. The account also mentions Haritmaṇimāyā-kuñja, a grove of illusion on the southern side of Śyāma-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gauravana
summary: This forest is named after Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who rested beneath a large banyan tree here during His visits to this part of Vṛndāvana after arriving in Mathurā in 1515.
body: This forest is named after Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who rested beneath a large banyan tree here during His visits to this part of Vṛndāvana after arriving in Mathurā in 1515. He often rested here, taking in the sights and sounds of the forest and the fragrance of the trees. It is also home to the samādhis of Vakreśvara Paṇḍita, Subuddhi Rāya, Rāmadāsa Abhirāma Dāsa, Śikhi Māhiti and others, including that of Gopāla-guru Gosvāmī, whom Caitanya Mahāprabhu affectionately named.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gaurikā-sarovara
summary: This lake in passing, as one of the beautiful lakes listed in a verse describing those around Govardhana Hill.
body: This lake in passing, as one of the beautiful lakes listed in a verse describing those around Govardhana Hill. The verse includes Śrī-sarovara, Brahma-sarovara, Kadamba-khaṇḍa-sarovara, Rudra-sarovara and many others. Tradition uses the verse to glorify these transcendental lakes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gaurī-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake is associated with Candrāvalī, as Rādhā's rival frequents it in the way Śrī Rādhā frequents Rādhā-kuṇḍa.
body: This lake is associated with Candrāvalī, as Rādhā's rival frequents it in the way Śrī Rādhā frequents Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Devotional accounts recount how Kṛṣṇa, asked by Padmā to pause here and reassure her friend Candrāvalī, walked through the aśoka forest between Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa and Gaurī-kuṇḍa, and how Padmā schemed to draw Kṛṣṇa toward Candrāvalī. Devotees of Rādhā visit to hear the pastime with devotion to Rādhā and respect for Candrāvalī, but do not cultivate devotion to Candrāvalī herself.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gaurī-tīrtha
summary: This place, where Rādhā was taught the mantras for worshipping Gaurī by Paurṇamāsī, is the setting for a scheme in which Abhimanyu asked Candrāvalī's friend Padmā to spy on it for Kṛṣṇa's presence.
body: This place, where Rādhā was taught the mantras for worshipping Gaurī by Paurṇamāsī, is the setting for a scheme in which Abhimanyu asked Candrāvalī's friend Padmā to spy on it for Kṛṣṇa's presence. Devotional accounts recount how Lalitā and Vṛndā walked towards Kṛṣṇa from Gaurī-tīrtha, leading to a confrontation between the rival gopī camps. Tradition closes by urging devotees who visit to beg for a place in the loving pastimes of Rādhā and Śyāmasundara.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gayā-kuṇḍa
summary: The personified Gayā resides at this lake along with the sage Agastya Muni, and people offer water or piṇḍa here for the progress of their forefathers.
body: The personified Gayā resides at this lake along with the sage Agastya Muni, and people offer water or piṇḍa here for the progress of their forefathers. When Nanda Mahārāja was about to offer oblations for his forefathers, Kṛṣṇa persuaded the family to visit Kāmyavana, and there He brought His father and uncles to Gayā-kuṇḍa so that the elders felt their duty had been properly done. Its sanctity equals Gayā-tīrtha because Kṛṣṇa's footprint is present on nearby Candrasena Hill.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gayā-tīrtha
summary: This is the famous place where Lord Viṣṇu killed the demon Gayā by stepping on him, and the demon's body was transformed into a series of hills that pilgrims still visit.
body: This is the famous place where Lord Viṣṇu killed the demon Gayā by stepping on him, and the demon's body was transformed into a series of hills that pilgrims still visit. Kṛṣṇa created an even more sacred Gayā in Kāmyavana with the same lotus feet, marked by the footprints on Candrasena Hill. Lord Caitanya, Lord Nityānanda, Advaita Ācārya, Mādhavendra Purī, Madhvācārya and the Gosvāmīs are all said to have had darśana of those footprints.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gaṅgā-kuṇḍa
summary: This lake lies not far from Praskandana-kuṇḍa, where Kṛṣṇa invoked the Ganges for the sake of His companions.
body: This lake lies not far from Praskandana-kuṇḍa, where Kṛṣṇa invoked the Ganges for the sake of His companions. A bath here is equal to one hundred baths in the Ganges River itself. It also records that Lord Caitanya, during His visit to Vṛndāvana, came to Dvādaśāditya-ṭīlā and appreciated its secluded and sacred atmosphere.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gaṇeśa-ghāṭa
summary: Also called Vighnarāja-ghāṭa, this ghāṭa lies on the Yamunā next to the secluded Koṭi-ghāṭa, the bathing place closest downstream from Akrūra-ghāṭa.
body: Also called Vighnarāja-ghāṭa, this ghāṭa lies on the Yamunā next to the secluded Koṭi-ghāṭa, the bathing place closest downstream from Akrūra-ghāṭa. By Lord Nṛsiṁha's grace Gaṇeśa removes all obstacles to pure devotion and bestows freedom from sins and miseries. It also notes that this is a good place to scatter the ashes of departed souls into the Yamunā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gendokhara-kuṇḍa
summary: This lakeside meadow lies along the old access road going south in Vraja, where Kṛṣṇa played ball with Śrī Rādhā and Her girlfriends, not with Balarāma and the cowherd boys.
body: This lakeside meadow lies along the old access road going south in Vraja, where Kṛṣṇa played ball with Śrī Rādhā and Her girlfriends, not with Balarāma and the cowherd boys. Just behind it is Kokilavana, where Kṛṣṇa is known as Kokila-bihārī, and where He and Rādhā wandered during the rāsa dance while He inspired the cuckoos to sing.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Ghaṇṭābharaṇa-ghāṭa
summary: This ghāṭa lies downstream from Brahma-tīrtha among the bathing places of Mathurā, and tradition says that bathing here leads one to the planet of the sun god.
body: This ghāṭa lies downstream from Brahma-tīrtha among the bathing places of Mathurā, and tradition says that bathing here leads one to the planet of the sun god. It is named because a bell (ghaṇṭā) is rung here to wake Lord Viṣṇu, who rests at Viśrāma-ghāṭa. Because Viṣṇu is said to sleep during the four-month period of cāturmāsya, people do not travel or perform Vedic sacrifices at that time.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Ghoṣarāṇī-kuṇḍa
summary: Among the Gopa-kuṇḍas in the Kāmyavana area, this lake is where Mother Yaśodā's brother Yaśodara arranged the marriage of his daughter Ghoṣarāṇī.
body: Among the Gopa-kuṇḍas in the Kāmyavana area, this lake is where Mother Yaśodā's brother Yaśodara arranged the marriage of his daughter Ghoṣarāṇī. Many kuṇḍas recorded in scripture have not been mapped or detailed, and pilgrims may find remnants of them. This lake is mentioned mainly in passing.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Go-ghāṭa
summary: In Kāmyavana, this ghāṭa lies on the western side of the expansive Vimala-kuṇḍa, where Kṛṣṇa's cows drink while He tends them and sports with His friends.
body: In Kāmyavana, this ghāṭa lies on the western side of the expansive Vimala-kuṇḍa, where Kṛṣṇa's cows drink while He tends them and sports with His friends. Elsewhere, the account describes Go-ghāṭa, also called Gopāla-ghāṭa, as a sheltered clearing between Varāha-ghāṭa and the place where Kṛṣṇa chastised the serpent Kāliya at nearby Kāliya-ghāṭa. Nārada Muni told King Bahulāśva a pastime of Vimala-kuṇḍa in which Kṛṣṇa housed ten million wives within its precincts.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Go-kuṇḍa
summary: This small lake lies on the edge of Śyāma-ḍhāk forest, where Kṛṣṇa and the cowherd boys drink deeply from its clear, sweet water when they bring their cows here.
body: This small lake lies on the edge of Śyāma-ḍhāk forest, where Kṛṣṇa and the cowherd boys drink deeply from its clear, sweet water when they bring their cows here. While the cows and boys rested on its banks, Kṛṣṇa would sneak away to meet Rādhā and a few intimate companions at nearby Rudravana. There they changed into bathing clothes and swam together in the refreshing lotus-filled water of Rudra-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gocaraṇavana
summary: This forest between Varāha-ghāṭa and Go-ghāṭa is named because Kṛṣṇa and His friends blissfully herded (caraṇa) their cows (go) along the riverside here.
body: This forest between Varāha-ghāṭa and Go-ghāṭa is named because Kṛṣṇa and His friends blissfully herded (caraṇa) their cows (go) along the riverside here. Go-ghāṭa is identified, also called Gopāla-ghāṭa, as a clearing linked to the chastisement of the serpent Kāliya at nearby Kāliya-ghāṭa. The account also notes that Gautama Muni chose Ramaṇa-reti near Varāha-ghāṭa as his residence.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gokarṇa-ghāṭa
summary: Nanda Mahārāja brought the cowherds to Ambikāvana on Śiva-rātri to worship Lord Śiva here, and Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma rode on his royal cart during the trip.
body: Nanda Mahārāja brought the cowherds to Ambikāvana on Śiva-rātri to worship Lord Śiva here, and Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma rode on his royal cart during the trip. Tradition recounts how a merchant named Gokarṇa decorated this site with gardens, performed austerities, and built the Śukeśvara temple for Śiva. The same account says that liberation, wealth, mastery in reciting Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and peace from ghosts can all be attained here by offering Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa a palmful of water with devotion.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gokarṇa-tīrtha
summary: Devotional accounts describe this as one of Vraja's great places of pilgrimage, lying downstream from Gaṇeśa-ghāṭa, where Gokarṇeśvara (Lord Śiva) stays with Satī and Pārvatī.
body: Devotional accounts describe this as one of Vraja's great places of pilgrimage, lying downstream from Gaṇeśa-ghāṭa, where Gokarṇeśvara (Lord Śiva) stays with Satī and Pārvatī. Lord Śiva is called the captain of the ship that carries us out of the ocean of troubles. Not all itineraries include it among the twenty-four bathing places, though it is commonly accepted as a place of great spiritual significance.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gokula-dhāma
summary: This is one of the auspicious names of Vṛndāvana, along with Goṣṭha and Vraja, as quoted from the Śrī Vraja-rīti-cintāmaṇi.
body: This is one of the auspicious names of Vṛndāvana, along with Goṣṭha and Vraja, as quoted from the Śrī Vraja-rīti-cintāmaṇi. Such names are often used informally in general ways. It also explains that the inner parikrama of Vraja is recommended for pilgrims who want to remember Kṛṣṇa's pastimes by visiting as many sacred places as they can.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gokula-mahāvana
summary: The name of this village is linked to the Mahāvana forest that covers much of this shore of the Yamunā, and the account recounts how Vasudeva carried baby Kṛṣṇa through the stormy night past Mūtra-sthāna on the way to Gokula.
body: The name of this village is linked to the Mahāvana forest that covers much of this shore of the Yamunā, and the account recounts how Vasudeva carried baby Kṛṣṇa through the stormy night past Mūtra-sthāna on the way to Gokula. When Lord Caitanya visited, He went from Khelā-tīrtha to Bhadravana and then to Gokula-mahāvana, where forest animals followed Him and He became absorbed in the mood of Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa. Tradition notes that the old village was largely destroyed when Mahmud of Ghazni sacked Mathurā and Gokula.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gomatī-ghāṭa
summary: Gomatī-ghāṭa is a place on the shore of Gomatī-kuṇḍa, reached from Kośīvana.
body: Gomatī-ghāṭa is a place on the shore of Gomatī-kuṇḍa, reached from Kośīvana. When Nanda Mahārāja's friends doubted Kṛṣṇa, He led the elders to the lake and asked them to look into it, and they saw the wonders of Kuśasthalī, including the ocean, Gomatī-ghāṭa and Dvārakā. From then on the Vraja-vāsīs regarded a visit to Gomatī-kuṇḍa and Kośīkalā as equal to a pilgrimage to Dvārakā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gomatī-kuṇḍa
summary: Gomatī-kuṇḍa is a lake near Kośīkalā (Kuśasthalī) where the gopīs went on pilgrimage, and where Kṛṣṇa joined them on the road by Sevā-kuñja on the pretext of inspecting His father's grain stores.
body: Gomatī-kuṇḍa is a lake near Kośīkalā (Kuśasthalī) where the gopīs went on pilgrimage, and where Kṛṣṇa joined them on the road by Sevā-kuñja on the pretext of inspecting His father's grain stores. At the lake the gopīs, guided by brāhmaṇas, performed their prescribed rites, and because of this delay they arrived home late and Jaṭilā was angry with Rādhā. The lake is also the place where the Vraja-vāsīs saw Dvārakā and afterwards counted a visit to it as a pilgrimage to Dvārakā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gopavana
summary: Gopavana is an expansive area of Vraja where, after Kṛṣṇa subdued Kāliya, Nanda Mahārāja gave many cows to qualified brāhmaṇas and distributed wealth, grains and cows to the twice-born citizens to celebrate and avert further danger.
body: Gopavana is an expansive area of Vraja where, after Kṛṣṇa subdued Kāliya, Nanda Mahārāja gave many cows to qualified brāhmaṇas and distributed wealth, grains and cows to the twice-born citizens to celebrate and avert further danger. The boys' mock battles between Balarāma's and Kṛṣṇa's parties are recalled here, and the last pastime place is Na-grāma, meaning no village, where the gopīs searched in separation for Kṛṣṇa. The account also notes samādhis in New Vraja-dhāma's Gopavana of Parameśvara Dāsa, Sundarānanda Dāsa, Rāmānanda Vasu and Rāghava Paṇḍita.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gopāla-ghāṭa
summary: Gopāla-ghāṭa, also called Go-ghāṭa, is a clearing sheltered by a few trees, linked to Kṛṣṇa's chastisement of the hundred-hooded serpent Kāliya at nearby Kāliya-ghāṭa.
body: Gopāla-ghāṭa, also called Go-ghāṭa, is a clearing sheltered by a few trees, linked to Kṛṣṇa's chastisement of the hundred-hooded serpent Kāliya at nearby Kāliya-ghāṭa. After Kāliya was banished and Kṛṣṇa returned to shore, Nanda Mahārāja gave many cows in charity on the advice of brāhmaṇas. The forest before it, Gocaraṇavana, is where Kṛṣṇa and His friends herded their cows along the riverside.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gopāla-kuṇḍa
summary: Gopāla-kuṇḍa is one of the limbs of Govardhana Hill, identified as his ears.
body: Gopāla-kuṇḍa is one of the limbs of Govardhana Hill, identified as his ears. Gvāla-kuṇḍa is also known by this name. Tradition says that the mere touch of Gopāla-kuṇḍa, along with Govinda-kuṇḍa and other lakes on the hill, destroys every sin.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Gopīśvara-tīrtha
summary: Gopīśvara-tīrtha is the place on the bank of the Yamunā, associated with Vaṁśīvaṭa, where the gopīs worshipped Lord Śiva as their master (Īśvara) in order to attain Kṛṣṇa.
body: Gopīśvara-tīrtha is the place on the bank of the Yamunā, associated with Vaṁśīvaṭa, where the gopīs worshipped Lord Śiva as their master (Īśvara) in order to attain Kṛṣṇa. Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī daily worshipped at this tīrtha where the gopīs had worshipped. Devotees who aspire to the gopīs' love of Kṛṣṇa can also worship Gopīśvara Mahādeva.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Gosvāmī-ghāṭa
summary: Dāsa Gosvāmī-ghāṭa, on the northern shore of Rādhā-kuṇḍa adjoining Jāhnavā-ghāṭa, is named for the samādhi of Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī, the first resident of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.
body: Dāsa Gosvāmī-ghāṭa, on the northern shore of Rādhā-kuṇḍa adjoining Jāhnavā-ghāṭa, is named for the samādhi of Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī, the first resident of Rādhā-kuṇḍa. The samādhi lies near the groves of Lalitā, Viśākhā and Rūpa-mañjarī, and was placed there to fulfil his wish to live forever on the banks of Rādhā-kuṇḍa with his worshipable superiors.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Govinda-ghāṭa
summary: Govinda-ghāṭa is the shoreline of Rādhā-kuṇḍa between the groves of Viśākhā and Citrā-devī, lying north of Śṛṅgāra-vaṭa.
body: Govinda-ghāṭa is the shoreline of Rādhā-kuṇḍa between the groves of Viśākhā and Citrā-devī, lying north of Śṛṅgāra-vaṭa. Here Sanātana Gosvāmī once had a vision in which Rūpa Gosvāmī and Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī fell at his feet, and the three embraced, bathing one another in tears of affection. It is linked with two rāsa-līlā pastimes, one in which Kṛṣṇa returned to the gopīs and one in which He searched for Rādhā, and tradition says the area is also called Govinda-sthalī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Govinda-tīrtha
summary: Govinda-tīrtha is glorified in the Saura Purāṇa, as quoted by Rūpa Gosvāmī, as a great holy place very dear to Lord Viṣṇu, where the Deity Lord Govindasvāmī presides.
body: Govinda-tīrtha is glorified in the Saura Purāṇa, as quoted by Rūpa Gosvāmī, as a great holy place very dear to Lord Viṣṇu, where the Deity Lord Govindasvāmī presides. Devotees who bathe there and worship yearn for release from birth and death. It is linked with Govinda-kuṇḍa, which the scriptures also call Govindasvāmī-tīrtha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Govindasvāmī-tīrtha
summary: Govindasvāmī-tīrtha is the name by which scriptures also call Govinda-kuṇḍa, a lake that is part of the unfurling lotus of Govindajī's Yoga-pīṭha.
body: Govindasvāmī-tīrtha is the name by which scriptures also call Govinda-kuṇḍa, a lake that is part of the unfurling lotus of Govindajī's Yoga-pīṭha. Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmī engaged in bhajana there and prayed for Govindajī's mercy. A bath there guarantees liberation from birth and death for sincere Vaiṣṇavas.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Guhya-tīrtha
summary: Guhya-tīrtha is a bathing place in Mathurā where bathing reveals the secret (guhya) of the Vedas, which is to know Kṛṣṇa.
body: Guhya-tīrtha is a bathing place in Mathurā where bathing reveals the secret (guhya) of the Vedas, which is to know Kṛṣṇa. Freed of material contamination, one quickly attains the spiritual world. Lord Śiva never leaves this holy place, being absorbed there in meditating on Kṛṣṇa's pastimes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
