title: Mayūra-kuṇḍa
summary: Mayūra-kuṇḍa lies on the outskirts of Rādhā-kuṇḍa's town, where Kṛṣṇa took the form of a peacock to shun the Apsarās and proclaim the glories of the rāsa dance.
body: Mayūra-kuṇḍa lies on the outskirts of Rādhā-kuṇḍa's town, where Kṛṣṇa took the form of a peacock to shun the Apsarās and proclaim the glories of the rāsa dance. In Mayūravana, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa danced like peacocks while the gopīs cheered, and afterward they refreshed themselves in this lake. Devotees pray here to be freed from misconceptions about Kṛṣṇa's character and pastimes, and a temple to the Pāṇḍavas stands on its bank.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mañca-sthala
summary: Mañca-sthala is listed as the twenty-second of the bathing places in Mathurā, among sites such as Prayāga-tīrtha, Dhruva-ghāṭa, and Daśāśvamedha.
body: Mañca-sthala is listed as the twenty-second of the bathing places in Mathurā, among sites such as Prayāga-tīrtha, Dhruva-ghāṭa, and Daśāśvamedha. Some of these ghāṭas have more than one name and that some names have changed. It is mentioned mainly in passing.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Maṇi-karṇika-ghāṭa
summary: This small lake beside the temple of Kāmeśvara Mahādeva in Kāmyavana is known as Maṇi-karṇika-ghāṭa, and a bath here grants liberation to the sincere person.
body: This small lake beside the temple of Kāmeśvara Mahādeva in Kāmyavana is known as Maṇi-karṇika-ghāṭa, and a bath here grants liberation to the sincere person. Opposite the Pāṇḍavas' house, the temple was originally worshipped by the Pāṇḍavas and later installed by Vajranābha as the guardian of this forest. The presence of this ghāṭa indicates that Kāśī, another name for Vārāṇasī, is situated here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Maṇi-karṇika-kuṇḍa
summary: King Vṛṣabhānu and his wife, desiring offspring, came to Kāmyavana, prayed to Kāmeśvara Mahādeva, and bathed with great devotion in Maṇi-karṇika-kuṇḍa.
body: King Vṛṣabhānu and his wife, desiring offspring, came to Kāmyavana, prayed to Kāmeśvara Mahādeva, and bathed with great devotion in Maṇi-karṇika-kuṇḍa. Lord Mahādeva answered their prayers, and Mother Kīrtidā gave birth to three divine children: Śrīdāmā, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and Anaṅga-mañjarī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mohana-kuṇḍa
summary: Mohana-kuṇḍa lies next to Lalitā-kuṇḍa, and the two lakes appeared when Lalitā and Kṛṣṇa shared memories of their encounters with Rādhā.
body: Mohana-kuṇḍa lies next to Lalitā-kuṇḍa, and the two lakes appeared when Lalitā and Kṛṣṇa shared memories of their encounters with Rādhā. When Lalitā's lake overflowed, it formed another lake, which she named Mohana-kuṇḍa after Kṛṣṇa. After killing the demon Ariṣṭāsura, Kṛṣṇa bathed in both lakes, and when Rādhā insisted He was contaminated by the sin of killing a bull, He replied that He had already bathed in Lalitā's lake.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mohavana
summary: Mohavana is a forest near Parāsaulī village where the demigods were illusioned by seeing the rāsa dance.
body: Mohavana is a forest near Parāsaulī village where the demigods were illusioned by seeing the rāsa dance. Nearby are Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa, Baladeva's pastime place, and Gandharva-kuṇḍa, where the Gandharvas marvelled at Kṛṣṇa's divine singing. Devotional accounts describe Mohavana as a place where Mahāmāyā's illusions are overcome only by absorption in the wonders of Kṛṣṇa's ways.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mohinī-kuṇḍa
summary: At Mohinī-kuṇḍa in Kāmyavana, Kṛṣṇa revealed the pastime incarnation of His beauty to prove that Śrīmatī Rādhikā is the ultimate beauty, more beautiful even than His Mohinī form.
body: At Mohinī-kuṇḍa in Kāmyavana, Kṛṣṇa revealed the pastime incarnation of His beauty to prove that Śrīmatī Rādhikā is the ultimate beauty, more beautiful even than His Mohinī form. Draped in a golden sari and ornamented with diamonds, Mohinī-devī first stood alone under the moonlit sky and cast a spell over the cowherd girls. She then stood beside Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and the two beauties were compared side by side before the gopīs.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mokṣa-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake just outside Govardhana town, one of three places where Caitanya Mahāprabhu rested during His parikrama of Govardhana Hill, the others being Indra-kuṇḍa near Mānasī-gaṅgā and Sūrya-kuṇḍa at Yatipura.
body: A lake just outside Govardhana town, one of three places where Caitanya Mahāprabhu rested during His parikrama of Govardhana Hill, the others being Indra-kuṇḍa near Mānasī-gaṅgā and Sūrya-kuṇḍa at Yatipura. His example teaches that a pilgrim should rest when weary or in pain, and parikrama should avoid practices that obstruct absorption in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes and thoughts of the dhāma. Beyond that, the accounts say little about the lake itself.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mokṣa-tīrtha
summary: A bathing ghāṭa in Mathurā, eleventh in the list of twenty-four, lying downstream from Ṛṣi-tīrtha where the seven sages Marīci, Atri, Aṅgirā, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha performed austerities.
body: A bathing ghāṭa in Mathurā, eleventh in the list of twenty-four, lying downstream from Ṛṣi-tīrtha where the seven sages Marīci, Atri, Aṅgirā, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha performed austerities. Its name means it bestows liberation, which here is described as bhakti, on those who bathe in its waters with full faith and without reservation. Tradition adds that the sages' five-thousand-year-old deities are still worshipped nearby.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Motī-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake near Nandagrāma that is the setting of a pearl pastime.
body: A lake near Nandagrāma that is the setting of a pearl pastime. Kṛṣṇa, to teach the gopīs a lesson after they refused Him pearl necklaces for His cows at Dīpāvalī, sowed a whole field with pearls here and soon harvested baskets of them. When the gopīs copied Him at Muktā-kuṇḍa near Varṣāṇā and failed, they had to bargain with Kṛṣṇa for pearls, and tradition says those negotiations can still be heard at Motī-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Muktā-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake in Nandagrāma, in a fertile field called Muktā-tīrtha, where Kṛṣṇa watered His cows and cultivated pearl-bearing creepers to the amazement of His parents and the gopīs.
body: A lake in Nandagrāma, in a fertile field called Muktā-tīrtha, where Kṛṣṇa watered His cows and cultivated pearl-bearing creepers to the amazement of His parents and the gopīs. The lake takes its name from these pearls and is also called Motī-kuṇḍa. Two pastimes are remembered here: one from the Garga-saṁhitā connected with Govardhana Hill, and one from Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī's Śrī Muktā-carita involving Rādhā and the gopīs insulting Kṛṣṇa over pearls for Dīpāvalī and a failed attempt at a second Muktā-kuṇḍa in Varṣāṇā. Another Muktā-kuṇḍa at Yāvaṭā is mentioned as the place where the gopīs decked Rādhā with pearls before she met Kṛṣṇa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Muktā-sarovara
summary: The lake that formed where Kṛṣṇa planted pearls, a pastime that ended the Vraja-vāsīs' doubts about His divinity.
body: The lake that formed where Kṛṣṇa planted pearls, a pastime that ended the Vraja-vāsīs' doubts about His divinity. After this episode the cowherd men accepted that Kṛṣṇa is the divine son of Nanda and never doubted it again. Donating a single pearl in charity at this lake brings the result of giving one hundred thousand times that number.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Muktā-tīrtha
summary: A fertile agricultural field behind a grove of banyan trees in Nandagrāma, whose soil is said to have mystic properties.
body: A fertile agricultural field behind a grove of banyan trees in Nandagrāma, whose soil is said to have mystic properties. Kṛṣṇa watered His cows at the clear lake in its centre, and in the surrounding fields He cultivated creepers that yielded pearls, astonishing His parents and the gopīs. The lake is therefore called Muktā-kuṇḍa or Motī-kuṇḍa, and tradition notes that two separate pastimes are associated with it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mādana-sukhadā-kuñja
summary: A grove at Rādhā-kuṇḍa that is one of Vraja's three special meeting places, or yoga-pīṭhas, along with Gupta-kuṇḍa and the jewelled temple at Govinda-sthalī.
body: A grove at Rādhā-kuṇḍa that is one of Vraja's three special meeting places, or yoga-pīṭhas, along with Gupta-kuṇḍa and the jewelled temple at Govinda-sthalī. These three are one in transcendental principle, so liberated souls who enter Gupta-kuṇḍa with full faith can emerge from Rādhā-kuṇḍa or from the Yamunā at Govinda-sthalī. Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa secretly meet on the shores of Gupta-kuṇḍa in the early morning.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mādhavānandada-kuñja
summary: An eight-petalled, lotus-shaped grove of eternally blossoming mādhavī creepers, northwest of the glorious Padmamandira.
body: An eight-petalled, lotus-shaped grove of eternally blossoming mādhavī creepers, northwest of the glorious Padmamandira. It is named because its appearance and fragrance give great pleasure to Mādhava, and Lalitā stores and offers her gifts of love to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa here. Anyone who enters it is said to feel exhilarated, as though flying on the back of a crane.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mādhurya-dhāma
summary: In traditional accounts Mādhurya-dhāma appears mainly as the title of a source cited in the notes, not as a place with its own pastime.
body: In traditional accounts Mādhurya-dhāma appears mainly as the title of a source cited in the notes, not as a place with its own pastime. The cited work is referenced in the notes for passages on Cakra-tīrtha and Gaurī-tīrtha. It is mentioned mostly in passing.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mādhurī-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake beyond the place where Rādhā decorated Kṛṣṇa with flowers, known as Saṅsā.
body: A lake beyond the place where Rādhā decorated Kṛṣṇa with flowers, known as Saṅsā. The residence of Rādhā's girlfriend Mādhurī is in the area around the lake. Devotional accounts describe Mādhurī-sakhī as renowned throughout Vraja for her skill in decorating Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa with flower ornaments.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mālyahāra-sarovara
summary: One of the splendid lakes glorified in a verse as lying in a circle around Govardhana Hill, along with Śrī-sarovara, Brahma-sarovara, Rudra-sarovara and others.
body: One of the splendid lakes glorified in a verse as lying in a circle around Govardhana Hill, along with Śrī-sarovara, Brahma-sarovara, Rudra-sarovara and others. The verse praises these lakes. Devotional accounts give no further pastime for this lake.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mālyahārī-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake on whose bank Rādhā and the gopīs string flower garlands, most of which are offered to Kṛṣṇa, with only a few used to worship the sun god at Sūrya-kuṇḍa.
body: A lake on whose bank Rādhā and the gopīs string flower garlands, most of which are offered to Kṛṣṇa, with only a few used to worship the sun god at Sūrya-kuṇḍa. Vṛndā-devī's Yoga-pīṭha residence is here, represented by a Tulasī greenhouse on the bank, and in winter Gopīśvara Mahādeva and Yogamāyā stay there with her. Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī's Pearl Story begins at this lake a day before Dīpāvalī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mānasa-pāvana
summary: A place near Vṛndāvana known for the bhajana of the Gosvāmīs and the ghāṭa of the same name.
body: A place near Vṛndāvana known for the bhajana of the Gosvāmīs and the ghāṭa of the same name. Tradition mentions that the ecstatic Sanātana Gosvāmī was visited there and that Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī used to go to Mānasa-pāvana-ghāṭa to associate with the other Gosvāmīs. It serves mainly as the setting for these episodes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mānasa-pāvana-ghāṭa
summary: A bathing ghāṭa on the bank of Śyāma-kuṇḍa, behind Govinda-ghāṭa and near Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī's residence.
body: A bathing ghāṭa on the bank of Śyāma-kuṇḍa, behind Govinda-ghāṭa and near Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī's residence. Five trees here were revealed to Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī to be the Pāṇḍavas performing bhajana. Rūpa, Raghunātha and Sanātana Gosvāmī met here, and the account recounts Sanātana's ecstatic trance, after which he told Rūpa that Rādhā confirmed Rūpa's description of Her hair. The area is also linked to the cottages built for the Gosvāmīs after two incidents involving Raghunātha Dāsa and Sanātana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Māra-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake on the outskirts of Yatipura, where Mādhavendra Purī kept Gopāla's granary.
body: A lake on the outskirts of Yatipura, where Mādhavendra Purī kept Gopāla's granary. Grain was husked and cleansed there before being sent to the Lord's kitchen, and the pounding and threshing wore a hollow in the ground that rain filled into a lake. The locals named it Māra-kuṇḍa, the lake formed by beating (māra) grain.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Mārava-grāma
summary: A village on the bank of the Yamunā in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, known as the āśrama of the sage Mārkaṇḍeya Ṛṣi.
body: A village on the bank of the Yamunā in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, known as the āśrama of the sage Mārkaṇḍeya Ṛṣi. After seven manvantaras, which span two days of Brahmā, Mārkaṇḍeya came here and understood that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme, and he is cited as the exemplar of determined faith. Śiva blessed him to live until the end of this day of Brahmā, and tradition says he still often resides on a hill in Mārava.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Māyāpur-Vṛndāvana
summary: Devotional accounts mention Māyāpur-Vṛndāvana only in passing, as the name of an annual festival in Vṛndāvana in 1976.
body: Devotional accounts mention Māyāpur-Vṛndāvana only in passing, as the name of an annual festival in Vṛndāvana in 1976. At that festival Śrīla Prabhupāda answered the question of the most confidential service, saying it is the service of the pūjārīs.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Māṭhavana
summary: A small forest where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma played with Their friends while the cows grazed on its pastures.
body: A small forest where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma played with Their friends while the cows grazed on its pastures. Three accounts explain its name: from the clay soil (māṭha) used to make pots, from a pot of buttermilk (māṭhā) that Kṛṣṇa knocked over while stealing milk products, and from its pastures (māṭha). It is also said that a drop of Mahādeva's semen fell here when Śiva, bewildered by Kṛṣṇa's Mohinī-mūrti, chased after Her.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Na-grāma
summary: A pastime place in Gopavana in New Vraja-dhāma, whose name means no village.
body: A pastime place in Gopavana in New Vraja-dhāma, whose name means no village. Once the gopīs, feeling intense separation, searched for Kṛṣṇa and despairingly cried out, No (na) Kṛṣṇa, so the place became Na-grāma. They then sat down and took to saṅkīrtana of Kṛṣṇa's names, and Kṛṣṇa appeared in their midst, though by then they felt mistreated and indignant.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nanda-ghāṭa
summary: A bathing ghāṭa on the Yamunā north of Cīra-ghāṭa, near the place called Bhaya.
body: A bathing ghāṭa on the Yamunā north of Cīra-ghāṭa, near the place called Bhaya. Here Varuṇa's servants kidnapped Nanda Mahārāja when he came to bathe and break his Ekādaśī fast on Dvādaśī, and the residents of Vṛndāvana, seeing this, called out to Kṛṣṇa in fear. Nanda later completed his vow and returned home with his two sons. The account also recounts that Jīva Gosvāmī lamented his offence at Nanda-ghāṭa until Sanātana Gosvāmī found him there.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nanda-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake beside Yaśodā-kuṇḍa at the foot of Nandīśvara Hill, where Nanda Mahārāja bathes every morning and chants the Gāyatrī mantra while his sons splash him.
body: A lake beside Yaśodā-kuṇḍa at the foot of Nandīśvara Hill, where Nanda Mahārāja bathes every morning and chants the Gāyatrī mantra while his sons splash him. In a shady grove beside it is Nanda-baiṭhaka, where Nanda and the elders of Vraja sit and discuss matters of concern to Vraja and Kṛṣṇa. When Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma are awake, Nanda brings Them to this lake to bathe, just as Yaśodā does at her own lake.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nava-ghāṭa
summary: The last bathing place upstream from Viśrāma-ghāṭa in Mathurā, also called Asi-kuṇḍa.
body: The last bathing place upstream from Viśrāma-ghāṭa in Mathurā, also called Asi-kuṇḍa. Some guides revere it as the main bathing place in Mathurā because of the pastimes connected with it. Devotional accounts recount King Sumati, who went on pilgrimage to Mathurā's holy places, returned to Godhead after his austerities, and was followed by his son Vimati, though the account is cut off there.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nava-Vṛndāvana
summary: A replica of Vṛndāvana built by Viśvakarmā at the request of Saṁjñā, so that the mood of Vraja could continue at Dvārakā.
body: A replica of Vṛndāvana built by Viśvakarmā at the request of Saṁjñā, so that the mood of Vraja could continue at Dvārakā. Saṁjñā did this because Rādhā was to appear as Kṛṣṇa's queen Satyabhāmā there, arranged through Satrājit's worship of the sun god. The sun god gave Satrājit the jewel of Śaṅkhacūḍa and Satyabhāmā-devī in return.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Navadvīpa-dhāma
summary: The holy abode of Lord Caitanya, which Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura glorified in his Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya.
body: The holy abode of Lord Caitanya, which Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura glorified in his Navadvīpa-dhāma-māhātmya. It serves as a model of dhāma-māhātmya, alongside Rūpa Gosvāmī's Mathurā-māhātmya. Tradition describes how Jīva Gosvāmī, led by Lord Nityānanda on a parikrama of Navadvīpa, received Caitanya Mahāprabhu's blessing to go to Vṛndāvana, where Caitanya appeared to him in a dream on the way to Vṛndāvana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Navagrāma
summary: A garden beyond Rādhā-kuṇḍa, also called Kuñjera or Kuñjara because of its many groves.
body: A garden beyond Rādhā-kuṇḍa, also called Kuñjera or Kuñjara because of its many groves. It is the setting of a pastime in which the gopīs formed themselves into a special elephant, and Kṛṣṇa climbed into a tree, mounted the gopī-elephant and used His flute as a goad to guide it through the garden. This shows Kṛṣṇa's supremacy, and also that to taste pure love He becomes subordinate to His devotees.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Navāla-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake among the lakes around Govardhana Hill, said to be filled with the liquid form of the divine couple's love.
body: A lake among the lakes around Govardhana Hill, said to be filled with the liquid form of the divine couple's love. In New Vraja-dhāma, Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa is also called Navāla-kuṇḍa, and beside it lies Apsarā-kuṇḍa in a secluded forest at the foot of Nṛsiṁha-ṭīlā. The name Navāla is explained by Kṛṣṇa, the eternal youth (nava), having come forth again from the waters of Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa, and anyone who bathes in these lakes without offence is said to be filled with ecstatic love.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: New-Vraja-dhāma
summary: Devotional accounts mention New-Vraja-dhāma mainly in passing, in a discussion of the pearl hanging from Kṛṣṇa's nose.
body: Devotional accounts mention New-Vraja-dhāma mainly in passing, in a discussion of the pearl hanging from Kṛṣṇa's nose. Śyāma has such an ornament in New-Vraja-dhāma, and Kṛṣṇa's nose is most attractive when He is in great ecstasy.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nikuñja
summary: Nikuñja is remembered mainly through the forest Nikuñjavana and the goddess Nikuñjavidyā, whom Vṛndā introduces as the goddess of Bhāṇḍīravana, her younger sister and the guardian of a treasure chest.
body: Nikuñja is remembered mainly through the forest Nikuñjavana and the goddess Nikuñjavidyā, whom Vṛndā introduces as the goddess of Bhāṇḍīravana, her younger sister and the guardian of a treasure chest. When Rādhā sat beside Nikuñjavidyā in the temple, the goddess stayed silent, and afterwards Kṛṣṇa, still dressed as Nikuñjavidyā but speaking in His own voice, eased Rādhā's anxiety by saying its sharp edge had been removed.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nikuñja-mandira
summary: A resting grove at the northeastern end of the garden called Hārayola, beside a tranquil Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa where the divine couple play games such as dice.
body: A resting grove at the northeastern end of the garden called Hārayola, beside a tranquil Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa where the divine couple play games such as dice. Rādhā once defeated Kṛṣṇa so thoroughly at dice that He was humiliated, and Lalitā cheered Him up by proposing a game of loving pastimes. Baḍa-baṭhain and this area inspire the leaders of New Vraja-dhāma in their own meetings.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nikuñjavana
summary: A forest containing Sevā-kuñja, where Kṛṣṇa danced the rāsa dance by moonlight after the gopīs had made Him reappear with their songs.
body: A forest containing Sevā-kuñja, where Kṛṣṇa danced the rāsa dance by moonlight after the gopīs had made Him reappear with their songs. Tradition describes Cupid entering a garden of Nikuñjavana to test Kṛṣṇa's self-control, and Kṛṣṇa leading Rādhā and the gopīs to see Ramaṇa-retī and the Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma tree.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
coordinate_source: Google Maps saved places export (via holy_places.xlsx)

title: Nimavana
summary: A forest of nima trees facing Sauṅkarāi, where the elderly gopīs embraced and worshipped Kṛṣṇa after He lifted Govardhana Hill.
body: A forest of nima trees facing Sauṅkarāi, where the elderly gopīs embraced and worshipped Kṛṣṇa after He lifted Govardhana Hill. The place was earlier called Nirmañcana-grāma, and the name has since become Nima-grāma. The ācārya Nimbārka lived here after Kṛṣṇa's disappearance and worshipped Kṛṣṇa there, and tradition notes that the forest is now some distance from Govardhana because the hill has shrunk.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nirmañcana-grāma
summary: The earlier name of the village now called Nima-grāma.
body: The earlier name of the village now called Nima-grāma. The elderly gopīs worshipped Kṛṣṇa with their love after Indra's deluge, offering ārati lamps with their tears, so the area was named Nirmañcana-grāma after this worship. Over time the name changed to Nima-grāma.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nityānanda-vaṭa
summary: Another name for Śṛṅgāra-vaṭa, the banyan tree on the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa decorated Rādhā and the cowherd boys decorated Him.
body: Another name for Śṛṅgāra-vaṭa, the banyan tree on the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa decorated Rādhā and the cowherd boys decorated Him. Lord Nityānanda lived here absorbed in remembrance of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes while He waited to join Caitanya Mahāprabhu in Navadvīpa, which is why it is also called Nityānanda-vaṭa. Both the gopas and gopīs visit this tree to dress and ornament one another.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nivāraṇa-ghāṭa
summary: The stairs on the bank of the Yamunā named for the place where Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī checked Kṛṣṇa's romantic advances.
body: The stairs on the bank of the Yamunā named for the place where Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī checked Kṛṣṇa's romantic advances. The forest there is revered as Nivāraṇavana. Nāma-saṅkīrtana in Nivāraṇavana removes every obstacle to spiritual advancement.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nivāraṇavana
summary: A forest revered because Rādhā checked (nivāraṇa) Kṛṣṇa's romantic advances, so that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa often meet with many obstacles.
body: A forest revered because Rādhā checked (nivāraṇa) Kṛṣṇa's romantic advances, so that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa often meet with many obstacles. It stands near Vihāravana, where Kṛṣṇa once played His mystic flute and attracted Rādhā, and then returned to repeat the melody. Nāma-saṅkīrtana here removes all obstacles to spiritual advancement.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nāga-tīrtha
summary: A holy bathing place in Mathurā, named for the bell (ghaṇṭā) rung there to wake Lord Viṣṇu, who rests at Viśrāma-ghāṭa during cāturmāsya.
body: A holy bathing place in Mathurā, named for the bell (ghaṇṭā) rung there to wake Lord Viṣṇu, who rests at Viśrāma-ghāṭa during cāturmāsya. Bathing there is said to award a journey to Vaikuṇṭha, and dying there brings liberation from birth and death. The immortal snake Ananta protects the dhāma from here, and once appeared to shelter Vasudeva and the infant Kṛṣṇa on their way to Gokula.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nārāyaṇa-sarovara
summary: A lake in the Govardhana area on the bank of which Kṛṣṇa hid when the gopīs searched for Him to revive the swooning Rādhā, near the cave He entered to lift Govardhana Hill.
body: A lake in the Govardhana area on the bank of which Kṛṣṇa hid when the gopīs searched for Him to revive the swooning Rādhā, near the cave He entered to lift Govardhana Hill. A temple of Caturbhuja, a four-armed Deity of Kṛṣṇa, stands on its bank, and the entrance to the cave is at the back wall of the temple. Tradition says that at Paīṭhā, Nārāyaṇa-sarovara marks where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa finally met, and Bankhaṇḍī Mahādeva guards the western side of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nīla-kuñja
summary: A pavilion at Rādhā-kuṇḍa whose sapphires give it a blackish hue, so Kṛṣṇa is camouflaged there.
body: A pavilion at Rādhā-kuṇḍa whose sapphires give it a blackish hue, so Kṛṣṇa is camouflaged there. When Jaṭilā came looking for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa after a rumour, she saw only the demure Rādhā, praised her chastity and left after cursing the rumour-mongers. Nearby, behind the western bathing ghāṭa, is the crimson grove of Tuṅgavidyā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nīlācala-dhāma
summary: The eternal abode of Lord Jagannātha at Purī, where He resides with Balarāma and Subhadrā-devī, as recited in the morning prayers quoted in devotional literature.
body: The eternal abode of Lord Jagannātha at Purī, where He resides with Balarāma and Subhadrā-devī, as recited in the morning prayers quoted in devotional literature. Devotees there perform kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtana in the mellow of ecstatic love. It is mentioned as a place of worship in devotional accounts's prayers rather than for any pastime.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nīpa-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake between Govinda-kuṇḍa and the parikrama path, surrounded by an area called Droṇa-kṣetra because Kṛṣṇa once served yogurt to the cowherd boys in cup-shaped leaves from its trees.
body: A lake between Govinda-kuṇḍa and the parikrama path, surrounded by an area called Droṇa-kṣetra because Kṛṣṇa once served yogurt to the cowherd boys in cup-shaped leaves from its trees. The boys rested on its banks while their cows grazed in Surabhivana, and the place came to be called Droṇa-tīrtha. Devotees who give yogurt in charity, or drink yogurt from a leaf-cup and bow to Girirāja, will return to Goloka and never fall.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nīpavana
summary: A forest west of Dāmodaravana that contains the secluded Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa play in the water in summer, and the samādhi of Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.
body: A forest west of Dāmodaravana that contains the secluded Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa play in the water in summer, and the samādhi of Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī. Earlier in devotional accounts, when the gopīs were walking home, Kṛṣṇa pointed them along a secluded path through Nīpavana to Kośīkalā to avoid the village. Tradition says the cows grazed in nearby Nīpavana while Kṛṣṇa, restless for Rādhā, went off to Kāmaravana to wait for her.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa
summary: Devotional accounts mention Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa mainly in passing, listing it among the lakes of the Kāmyavana area alongside Veda-kuṇḍa, Dāmodara-kuṇḍa, Gandharva-kuṇḍa, Arghya-kuṇḍa and Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa.
body: Devotional accounts mention Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa mainly in passing, listing it among the lakes of the Kāmyavana area alongside Veda-kuṇḍa, Dāmodara-kuṇḍa, Gandharva-kuṇḍa, Arghya-kuṇḍa and Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa. The surrounding notes cite Garga-saṁhitā and Caitanya-caritāmṛta but do not describe a specific pastime at this lake.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Padmamandira
summary: Padmamandira is the highest point of the lotus-palace of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa near Yoga-pīṭha and Rādhā-kuṇḍa, a three-storey turret from which the divine couple view the forest on one side and their two lakes on the other.
body: Padmamandira is the highest point of the lotus-palace of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa near Yoga-pīṭha and Rādhā-kuṇḍa, a three-storey turret from which the divine couple view the forest on one side and their two lakes on the other. The palace has hundreds of rooms with gold floors, crystal pillars, coral balconies and carved domes, and each room serves a distinct purpose in Their pastimes. Tradition presents it as a jewelled palace full of multifaceted bliss.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Papaḍavana
summary: Papaḍavana is a forest stretching from Ādibadrī-ghāṭa to Bhatrola, with Rāja-ghāṭa at its centre, once a landing where boats ferried people across the Yamunā when the river still flowed here.
body: Papaḍavana is a forest stretching from Ādibadrī-ghāṭa to Bhatrola, with Rāja-ghāṭa at its centre, once a landing where boats ferried people across the Yamunā when the river still flowed here. Kṛṣṇa liked to disguise Himself as a boatman there, and Rādhārāṇī and Her friends crossed the river with milk products for relatives. Tradition also recalls Vyāsa writing the Tenth Canto while residing in the Himalayas, transported to Ādibadrī-ghāṭa, and describes his own early visit to the site with his mother.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Paraśu-kuṇḍa
summary: Paraśu-kuṇḍa lies near Nandagrāma on the stretch of road where Kṛṣṇa departed on the chariot with Balarāma for Mathurā.
body: Paraśu-kuṇḍa lies near Nandagrāma on the stretch of road where Kṛṣṇa departed on the chariot with Balarāma for Mathurā. Kṛṣṇa promised to return "the day after tomorrow (paraśu)," which gave the road its name, and the gopīs' cries are said still to echo there and stir the waves of the lake. Vaiṣṇavas who visit call out "Govinda! Dāmodara, Mādhava!" as a remembrance of the gopīs' separation.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Paurṇamāsī-kuṇḍa
summary: Paurṇamāsī-kuṇḍa is in a secluded part of a wood near Nandagrāma, along the route Kṛṣṇa took on His nocturnal visits toward Saṅketavana and Rādhā-vana.
body: Paurṇamāsī-kuṇḍa is in a secluded part of a wood near Nandagrāma, along the route Kṛṣṇa took on His nocturnal visits toward Saṅketavana and Rādhā-vana. The Vraja-vāsīs built two cottages there, one for their guru Paurṇamāsī and one for her granddaughter Nāndīmukhī, who lived under the protection of Nanda Mahārāja. The caves in Nandīśvara Hill are also said to have been the residences of these two brāhmaṇīs.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pavitra-kuṇḍa
summary: Pavitra-kuṇḍa is in Mathurā near Potarā-kuṇḍa, the lake where Devakī washed Kṛṣṇa's diapers and the garments she wore at His birth.
body: Pavitra-kuṇḍa is in Mathurā near Potarā-kuṇḍa, the lake where Devakī washed Kṛṣṇa's diapers and the garments she wore at His birth. Local tradition holds that this lake was originally called Pavitra-kuṇḍa, and it once lay within Kaṁsa's palace compound, where Devakī and Vasudeva bathed while imprisoned. Tradition says that bathing in its pure water frees one of the sins of many lifetimes and bestows devotion that leads to vision of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Paya-grāma
summary: Paya-grāma is the village where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma's hungry cowherd friends went after Balarāma suggested asking pious villagers for milk.
body: Paya-grāma is the village where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma's hungry cowherd friends went after Balarāma suggested asking pious villagers for milk. The boys were given milk (payaḥ), which is how the village got its name. Nearby, Dadhi-grāma is where Kṛṣṇa once stole yogurt from the gopīs to please Himself and feed His friends.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pañca-pāṇḍava-ghāṭa
summary: Pañca-pāṇḍava-ghāṭa is a bathing landing on Śyāma-kuṇḍa, where Raghunātha Dāsa called off the removal of trees after King Yudhiṣṭhira appeared and said that he and his brothers lived in them, which is why the lake's shape is irregular.
body: Pañca-pāṇḍava-ghāṭa is a bathing landing on Śyāma-kuṇḍa, where Raghunātha Dāsa called off the removal of trees after King Yudhiṣṭhira appeared and said that he and his brothers lived in them, which is why the lake's shape is irregular. Just north is the Rādhā-Govinda temple, marking the divine couple's daily meeting place, and the jihvā-śilā, the tongue of Govardhana Hill. This spot is one of two places called the Yoga-pīṭha of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, the other being the saṅgama.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pañca-pāṇḍava-kuṇḍa
summary: Pañca-pāṇḍava-kuṇḍa lies inside the old city wall of Kāman, close to Dharma-kuṇḍa, so that the two are practically indistinguishable.
body: Pañca-pāṇḍava-kuṇḍa lies inside the old city wall of Kāman, close to Dharma-kuṇḍa, so that the two are practically indistinguishable. Here the pastime between the Pāṇḍavas and Yamarāja took place, though it is usually connected to the more familiar Dharma-kuṇḍa. Nearby, Pāṇḍava-kūpa is the well from which the sons of Pāṇḍu drew water and where Draupadī did her washing.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pañca-pāṇḍava-tīrtha
summary: Pañca-pāṇḍava-tīrtha is a site in Kāmyavana where, in a brāhmaṇa's house, deities of Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja and two of his brothers are served.
body: Pañca-pāṇḍava-tīrtha is a site in Kāmyavana where, in a brāhmaṇa's house, deities of Yudhiṣṭhira Mahārāja and two of his brothers are served. Tradition says the Pāṇḍavas lived here for part of their stay, and describes the deities as black and very tall, with Yudhiṣṭhira's presence making one bow down before him.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pañca-tīrtha-kuṇḍa
summary: Pañca-tīrtha-kuṇḍa is said to contain the waters of five sacred rivers, Gomatī, Narmadā, Sarayū, Vetra and Kāñcī, and five more holy places are said to reside on its bathing ghāṭas.
body: Pañca-tīrtha-kuṇḍa is said to contain the waters of five sacred rivers, Gomatī, Narmadā, Sarayū, Vetra and Kāñcī, and five more holy places are said to reside on its bathing ghāṭas. Bathing in it or taking its dust is said to equal visiting all ten places. The lake is also called Harideva-kuṇḍa, and because Kṛṣṇa and the gopas enjoyed playing ball here, the area is known as Kanduka-kṣetra.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Paśupāvana
summary: Paśupāvana is a forest south of Bhayarī, and within it is the grove Paśupā where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma hid from their cowherd friends during a game of hide-and-seek.
body: Paśupāvana is a forest south of Bhayarī, and within it is the grove Paśupā where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma hid from their cowherd friends during a game of hide-and-seek. Their clever cows caught Their scent, lowed, dug the earth and sniffed the bushes until the boys found the two brothers in the grove, where they were gleefully jumping up and down. Tradition also mentions nearby Kāyarika, where Kṛṣṇa lit up the forest with the effulgence of His body.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Phulvāri-kuṇḍa
summary: Phulvāri-kuṇḍa is a flower garden near Nandagrāma where Rādhā was picking flowers to string a garland for Kṛṣṇa when He appeared with His friends and then suddenly left.
body: Phulvāri-kuṇḍa is a flower garden near Nandagrāma where Rādhā was picking flowers to string a garland for Kṛṣṇa when He appeared with His friends and then suddenly left. Rādhā fainted, and Kṛṣṇa returned, touched her cheek and called out "Rādhā! I am here! Open Your eyes!" She revived, and He stayed for some time at this spot. Tradition describes Pāvana-sarovara, the foremost lake of Nandagrāma, where Caitanya Mahāprabhu bathed and where pilgrims first bathe before visiting Nanda-bhavana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pibana-kuṇḍa
summary: Pibana-kuṇḍa is one of the names of a sacred kadamba forest in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, also called Piyāla-kuṇḍa and Pāḍar-gaṅgā, in the area of Yāvaṭā and Kiśorī-kuñja.
body: Pibana-kuṇḍa is one of the names of a sacred kadamba forest in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, also called Piyāla-kuṇḍa and Pāḍar-gaṅgā, in the area of Yāvaṭā and Kiśorī-kuñja. Once, when Lalitā urged Kṛṣṇa to kiss Rādhā, He drank the nectar of Her lips and became intoxicated, which gives the place its name from the Sanskrit root piba, to drink. Rādhā planted a pārijāta tree on the bank of this lake and tended it until it blossomed.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pipāsavana
summary: Pipāsavana is a jungle at the edge of which stands Yogamāyā's temple, near Varṣāṇā, also called Piyāso by some.
body: Pipāsavana is a jungle at the edge of which stands Yogamāyā's temple, near Varṣāṇā, also called Piyāso by some. Here Kṛṣṇa became thirsty (pipāsā) while herding cows, and Balarāma brought Him a drink from Pyāsa-kuṇḍa. Tradition also mentions a mysterious ascetic, popularly called Jhariwale Bābā, whom he identifies as Aśvatthāmā, who constantly chants Kṛṣṇa's names here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Piyāla-kuṇḍa
summary: Piyāla-kuṇḍa is one of the names of the sacred kadamba forest in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, alongside Pibana-kuṇḍa and Pāḍar-gaṅgā, near Kiśorī-kuñja in Yāvaṭā.
body: Piyāla-kuṇḍa is one of the names of the sacred kadamba forest in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, alongside Pibana-kuṇḍa and Pāḍar-gaṅgā, near Kiśorī-kuñja in Yāvaṭā. In the pastime retold here, Lalitā urged Kṛṣṇa to kiss Rādhā and He drank the nectar of Her lips and became intoxicated. Rādhā planted a pārijāta tree on the lake's bank and tended it until it blossomed.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Potarā-kuṇḍa
summary: Potarā-kuṇḍa is a beautiful, expansive tank near Jñāna-bābara in Mathurā where Devakī washed the diapers (potarā) of Kṛṣṇa and the garments she wore while giving birth to Him.
body: Potarā-kuṇḍa is a beautiful, expansive tank near Jñāna-bābara in Mathurā where Devakī washed the diapers (potarā) of Kṛṣṇa and the garments she wore while giving birth to Him. It was originally within Kaṁsa's palace compound, and Devakī and Vasudeva bathed there while imprisoned. Local tradition holds that the lake was originally called Pavitra-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Prabhupādavana
summary: Prabhupādavana is the garden forest near Varṣāṇā Road, named in honour of Śrīla Prabhupāda's samādhi, and it includes the guesthouse representing the Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma Mandira at Ramaṇa-retī.
body: Prabhupādavana is the garden forest near Varṣāṇā Road, named in honour of Śrīla Prabhupāda's samādhi, and it includes the guesthouse representing the Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma Mandira at Ramaṇa-retī. The tamāla tree in that temple's courtyard, which Śrīla Prabhupāda said was a meeting place of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and whose luxuriant growth would indicate the spiritual health of his disciples. In the corner of the forest is Gajendra-mokṣaṇa-kuṇḍa, representing the lake where the deliverance of Gajendra is enacted yearly.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Prabhāsa-tīrtha
summary: Prabhāsa-tīrtha is the holy place where the Yadus were sent in Dvārakā after omens of ruin appeared and the demigods had departed.
body: Prabhāsa-tīrtha is the holy place where the Yadus were sent in Dvārakā after omens of ruin appeared and the demigods had departed. Kṛṣṇa reminded the wise Yadus of the brāhmaṇas' curse and told them that charity, bathing at Prabhāsa-tīrtha and gifts to Vaiṣṇavas would carry them safely across these dangers. Tradition understood from this that the Lord intended to return to Vaikuṇṭha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Prahlāda-kuṇḍa
summary: Prahlāda-kuṇḍa is at Phalain, near Kośīkalā and off the official parikrama route, and is the home of the devotee Prahlāda Mahārāja.
body: Prahlāda-kuṇḍa is at Phalain, near Kośīkalā and off the official parikrama route, and is the home of the devotee Prahlāda Mahārāja. It is well known for the annual Holī festival held there, in which an effigy of Holikā is burnt at night and the next day revellers throw colours to celebrate Prahlāda's victory. The pastime is re-enacted because Prahlāda was protected by the Lord through his full dependence on Kṛṣṇa and the chanting of His names.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Prakaṭa-dhāma
summary: This section explains that Goloka Vṛndāvana, the aprakaṭa-dhāma, is the complete manifestation of Kṛṣṇa's spiritual potency, where material energy has no influence.
body: This section explains that Goloka Vṛndāvana, the aprakaṭa-dhāma, is the complete manifestation of Kṛṣṇa's spiritual potency, where material energy has no influence. The prakaṭa-dhāma is Bhauma Vṛndāvana, the same abode appearing in the material world during Kṛṣṇa's manifest pastimes. Because it appears in the material world, it sometimes seems to conform to material laws and does not always display its full powers.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pramodavana
summary: Pramodavana is a forest past Ghāṭā, linked with the village of Pramodana and the delight (pramoda) Kṛṣṇa gave the gopīs who came there searching for Him.
body: Pramodavana is a forest past Ghāṭā, linked with the village of Pramodana and the delight (pramoda) Kṛṣṇa gave the gopīs who came there searching for Him. When the gopīs combed the countryside for Him, He hid, and when they found Him they lay on the ground like dry leaves until Kṛṣṇa revived them by His touch and voice. Tradition mentions a deity of Sudāmā worshipped at Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa and Caraṇa-kuṇḍa, blessed by Kṛṣṇa's feet.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Praskandana-kuṇḍa
summary: Praskandana-kuṇḍa was formed from Kṛṣṇa's perspiration when the twelve sun gods surrounded Him on a cold morning and warmed Him until He perspired profusely, the perspiration flowing down the hill to form a small lake.
body: Praskandana-kuṇḍa was formed from Kṛṣṇa's perspiration when the twelve sun gods surrounded Him on a cold morning and warmed Him until He perspired profusely, the perspiration flowing down the hill to form a small lake. Tradition says bathing or worshipping the sun god there leads to the sun planet, and the rituals on a Sunday also fulfil desires. The place is now hidden from view and is called a gupta-tīrtha, though Lord Caitanya later visited it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Praskandana-sarovara
summary: Praskandana-sarovara is a lake formed from Kṛṣṇa's perspiration when the twelve suns shone on Him, and it is described in a verse of Dāsa Gosvāmī that tradition cites in worship of it.
body: Praskandana-sarovara is a lake formed from Kṛṣṇa's perspiration when the twelve suns shone on Him, and it is described in a verse of Dāsa Gosvāmī that tradition cites in worship of it. The site lies on the Varāha-ghāṭa to Keśī-ghāṭa stretch of the Yamunā, near Sūrya-ghāṭa. Further along past Sūrya-ghāṭa are Yugala-ghāṭa and Vihāra-ghāṭa, which are linked to the bathing and resting pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

title: Praskandana-tīrtha
summary: Praskandana-tīrtha is a rose garden on the bank of the Yamunā, once known as the foremost rose forest of Vṛndāvana.
body: Praskandana-tīrtha is a rose garden on the bank of the Yamunā, once known as the foremost rose forest of Vṛndāvana. When Rādhā first hinted of her love through a gopī messenger, Kṛṣṇa, with Madhumaṅgala, came here to scent His reply by extracting oil from the flowers and writing on rose petals. Tradition also notes another Praskandana-tīrtha in Kṛṣṇa Valley, and gardeners still grow aromatic roses here for garlands.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Prayāga-ghāṭa
summary: Prayāga-ghāṭa is a ghāṭa in Mathurā where Tīrtharāja, the king of holy places, stayed after realising that he had committed an offence by trying to exercise authority over Mathurā.
body: Prayāga-ghāṭa is a ghāṭa in Mathurā where Tīrtharāja, the king of holy places, stayed after realising that he had committed an offence by trying to exercise authority over Mathurā. Here pilgrims receive the benefit of all Vedic sacrifices, ancestors are liberated by offerings, and service to Kṛṣṇa ends the cycle of birth and death. Veṇī-mādhava's temple stands adjacent to this ghāṭa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Prayāga-tīrtha
summary: Prayāga-tīrtha is a holy place by the riverside in Mathurā, near Sudāmā's home, where worship bestows residence in heaven or Goloka according to one's desire.
body: Prayāga-tīrtha is a holy place by the riverside in Mathurā, near Sudāmā's home, where worship bestows residence in heaven or Goloka according to one's desire. The king of all holy places performed austerities here to atone for slighting Kṛṣṇa's abode, so those who have offended the dhāma can come here to beg forgiveness. The sage Pippalāyana was saved here from a demon by Lord Śiva, who has since been worshipped here as Pippaleśvara.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Puṣkara-tīrtha
summary: Puṣkara-tīrtha is cited to show that Lord Hari personally stays in Mathurā-maṇḍala, which is forty yojanas from it, and Bhauma Vṛndāvana cannot be matched by any other dhāma.
body: Puṣkara-tīrtha is cited to show that Lord Hari personally stays in Mathurā-maṇḍala, which is forty yojanas from it, and Bhauma Vṛndāvana cannot be matched by any other dhāma. Tradition also tells how Śūrpaṇakhā retired to Puṣkara-tīrtha after the war over Sītā, meditating on Lord Śiva underwater for ten thousand years, and Śiva promised that she would have Rāma as her husband at the end of Dvāpara-yuga. The section also tells of the brāhmaṇa Divadāsa, who was directed in a dream to stay in Navadvīpa instead of completing his pilgrimage to Puṣkara.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Puṣpavana
summary: Puṣpavana is the forest of ever-blooming flowers near Pañca-tīrtha-kuṇḍa, and at its heart lies Kusuma-sarovara, also called Sumanaḥ-sarovara.
body: Puṣpavana is the forest of ever-blooming flowers near Pañca-tīrtha-kuṇḍa, and at its heart lies Kusuma-sarovara, also called Sumanaḥ-sarovara. The sage Aṣṭāvakra's perfection is retold in an appendix, and Rādhā once picked flowers here while Kṛṣṇa, hidden on a campaka branch, bent it down for her. The Uddhava pastime also took place beside Kusuma-sarovara, where Uddhava appeared from the creepers in response to the kīrtana of Parīkṣit Mahārāja and Kṛṣṇa's wives.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pyāsa-kuṇḍa
summary: Pyāsa-kuṇḍa is a lake near Varṣāṇā, at the edge of Pipāsavana near Yogamāyā's temple, where Balarāma brought Kṛṣṇa a drink when He became thirsty while herding cows.
body: Pyāsa-kuṇḍa is a lake near Varṣāṇā, at the edge of Pipāsavana near Yogamāyā's temple, where Balarāma brought Kṛṣṇa a drink when He became thirsty while herding cows. Tradition also describes the ascetic Jhariwale Bābā, identified as Aśvatthāmā, who lives in the area and constantly chants Kṛṣṇa's names. The place is remembered mainly through this pastime.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāni-ghāṭa
summary: Pāni-ghāṭa is the Yamunā landing where Rādhā led the gopīs, on Kṛṣṇa's advice, to ask the river to part on the strength of His brahmacarya vow.
body: Pāni-ghāṭa is the Yamunā landing where Rādhā led the gopīs, on Kṛṣṇa's advice, to ask the river to part on the strength of His brahmacarya vow. The waters parted into two walls, the gopīs held hands and crossed, and the place is named for the parting of the waters (pāni). Tradition links it to the Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad pastime and notes that Ādibadrī-ghāṭa, where Kṛṣṇa revealed Himself as Badarī-nārāyaṇa, comes next.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāni-grāma
summary: Pāni-grāma, south of the dam on the Yamunā, is the residence of the sage Durvāsā Muni, where the gopīs fed him food they had brought after crossing at Pāni-ghāṭa.
body: Pāni-grāma, south of the dam on the Yamunā, is the residence of the sage Durvāsā Muni, where the gopīs fed him food they had brought after crossing at Pāni-ghāṭa. Some hold it as his birthplace or hermitage, and Durvāsā explained his vow and Kṛṣṇa's were unaffected by their deeds. Nearby is the āśrama of Parāśara Muni, and further upstream the home of the fisherman's daughter Satyavatī, mother of Vyāsa.

title: Pānīhārī-kuṇḍa
summary: Pānīhārī-kuṇḍa is a charming lake near Nandagrāma where Rādhārāṇī and Mother Rohiṇī cook in summer under bakula trees, and where Kṛṣṇa and the gopas take their meals and drink its water (pāni), the name being explained by the Sanskrit word hari for partaking.
body: Pānīhārī-kuṇḍa is a charming lake near Nandagrāma where Rādhārāṇī and Mother Rohiṇī cook in summer under bakula trees, and where Kṛṣṇa and the gopas take their meals and drink its water (pāni), the name being explained by the Sanskrit word hari for partaking. Uddhava bathed here and saw the gopīs gathered around his chariot. The water is so sweet that the Vraja-vāsīs come from all around to fetch drinking water, and Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā gaze at each other across the ghāṭa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāpamocana-kuṇḍa
summary: Pāpamocana-kuṇḍa lies to the east of Indra-dhvaja-tīrtha, and is famed, together with Ṛṇamocana-kuṇḍa to its west, for its sanctity, since devotees who bathe in them are freed from all vices.
body: Pāpamocana-kuṇḍa lies to the east of Indra-dhvaja-tīrtha, and is famed, together with Ṛṇamocana-kuṇḍa to its west, for its sanctity, since devotees who bathe in them are freed from all vices. Tradition recounts Kṛṣṇa's words that He would end the tradition of worshipping Indra and begin worshipping Him through Govardhana Hill. In Bhauma Vṛndāvana both lakes have been filled in, and Pāpamocana-kuṇḍa is now Govardhana town's bus station.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāpaḍīvana
summary: Pāpaḍīvana is a flowering forest south of Kanabāḍī, named for its central grove Pāpaḍī, where the gopīs decorated Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa with ornaments made of petals.
body: Pāpaḍīvana is a flowering forest south of Kanabāḍī, named for its central grove Pāpaḍī, where the gopīs decorated Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa with ornaments made of petals. Tradition recounts Kṛṣṇa accepting chipped rice from His friend in Kanabāḍī and blessing him with unlimited wealth, showing His regard for His devotees. Tradition presents these places as reasons to offer abundant flowers in the temples.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāvana
summary: Pāvana is the hill and palace area of Nanda-bhavana at Nandagrāma, with staircases on its sides, the north one leading Kṛṣṇa to Pāvana-sarovara and the west one used by Rādhā and her friends coming from Yāvaṭā.
body: Pāvana is the hill and palace area of Nanda-bhavana at Nandagrāma, with staircases on its sides, the north one leading Kṛṣṇa to Pāvana-sarovara and the west one used by Rādhā and her friends coming from Yāvaṭā. In a secluded forest to the southeast of Pāvana-sarovara the Vraja-vāsīs built a bhajana-kuṭīra for Sanātana Gosvāmī, and Kṛṣṇa once appeared to him as a cowherd boy carrying milk when he had no protection from the elements. Lord Caitanya later visited the deities found in a nearby cave, and Sanātana Gosvāmī moved them to the hilltop.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāśa-khela-ghāṭa
summary: Pāśa-khela-ghāṭa is a lakeshore on the western bank of Śyāma-kuṇḍa, reached along the path toward the grove of Vidagdha, and it is called Vallabha-ghāṭa by Vallabhācārya's followers.
body: Pāśa-khela-ghāṭa is a lakeshore on the western bank of Śyāma-kuṇḍa, reached along the path toward the grove of Vidagdha, and it is called Vallabha-ghāṭa by Vallabhācārya's followers. It is named for pāśa-khela, a dice game requiring skill and luck, which the gopī Sudevī excels at, and Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa play it almost daily in her kuñja. Tradition mentions Caitanya Mahāprabhu's visit to Kusuma-sarovara, where He embraced a stone of Girirāja in ecstasy.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāṇḍava-kuṇḍa
summary: Pāṇḍava-kuṇḍa is near Hoḍal, at the southern edge of Bhūlanvana, where the Pāṇḍavas are said to have lived incognito during their last year of exile.
body: Pāṇḍava-kuṇḍa is near Hoḍal, at the southern edge of Bhūlanvana, where the Pāṇḍavas are said to have lived incognito during their last year of exile. Tradition says they took pleasure in visiting Vṛndāvana-dhāma and lived in Kāman and Hoḍal while travelling through the forests of Vraja. Devotional accounts describe their presence here mainly as a historical footnote to the parikrama route.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pāṭalavana
summary: Pāṭalavana is a garden of pink roses, sometimes called Pāṭala, on the eastern petal of the Yoga-pīṭha, where Rādhā and the gopīs gather flowers and string garlands for the Lord.
body: Pāṭalavana is a garden of pink roses, sometimes called Pāṭala, on the eastern petal of the Yoga-pīṭha, where Rādhā and the gopīs gather flowers and string garlands for the Lord. In a shady grove at its centre the gopīs chatter sweetly about Kṛṣṇa's exploits while working under Rādhā's guidance. A coincidental parallel with a garden in New Vraja-dhāma.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pūrṇendu-kuñja
summary: Pūrṇendu-kuñja is the grove of Indulekhā in the southeastern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, named for its resemblance to the full moon.
body: Pūrṇendu-kuñja is the grove of Indulekhā in the southeastern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, named for its resemblance to the full moon. It is distinguished by its whiteness, with couches, platforms and pavilions of crystal and moonstone, and lotuses and trees with white leaves and flowers. Tradition describes it as far whiter than Lalitā's sub-grove Sitāmbuja.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pūtanā-uddhāra-sthala
summary: Pūtanā-uddhāra-sthala, meaning the place where Pūtanā was liberated, is the site where the demoness fell after she attempted to kill Kṛṣṇa.
body: Pūtanā-uddhāra-sthala, meaning the place where Pūtanā was liberated, is the site where the demoness fell after she attempted to kill Kṛṣṇa. It is mentioned mainly in notes, which describe Pūtanā's past life from Garga-saṁhitā and the Śrī Kṛṣṇa-kavaca mantra. The main text gives little more detail about this place.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa
summary: Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa, also called Navāla-kuṇḍa, is the lake at the tail of Govardhana Hill, described as the peacock-shaped hill's tail, and lies in a secluded forest at the foot of Nṛsiṁha-ṭīlā beside Apsarā-kuṇḍa.
body: Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa, also called Navāla-kuṇḍa, is the lake at the tail of Govardhana Hill, described as the peacock-shaped hill's tail, and lies in a secluded forest at the foot of Nṛsiṁha-ṭīlā beside Apsarā-kuṇḍa. Kṛṣṇa brings His girlfriends here to stage the rāsa dance. In the churning pastime the rāsa circle churned the milk of prema, with buttermilk flowing into Apsarā-kuṇḍa and the soft butter collecting in Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Pṛthu-kuṇḍa
summary: Pṛthu-kuṇḍa is at Māyāpur, where Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura excavated Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa beside it to commemorate Lord Caitanya's absorption in vraja-līlā.
body: Pṛthu-kuṇḍa is at Māyāpur, where Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura excavated Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa beside it to commemorate Lord Caitanya's absorption in vraja-līlā. He also built a small likeness of Govardhana Hill from a truckload of stones. The place is associated with the atmosphere of Bhauma Vṛndāvana rather than describing a pastime here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rabrī-kuṇḍa
summary: Rabrī-kuṇḍa is one of the lakes decorating Vatsavana, where the rabrī appeared when the gopas found piles of rabrī, yogurt and butter that they ate with gusto while praising Kṛṣṇa's flute.
body: Rabrī-kuṇḍa is one of the lakes decorating Vatsavana, where the rabrī appeared when the gopas found piles of rabrī, yogurt and butter that they ate with gusto while praising Kṛṣṇa's flute. Nearby Śaṅkara-kuṇḍa has a temple of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and bathing in these lakes washes away sins. Vatsavana is also where the cows and older gopas were overwhelmed by affection for calves that were expansions of Kṛṣṇa, after Brahmā had stolen the originals a year earlier.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rasānandada-kuñja
summary: Rasānandada-kuñja is the kuñja of Rasa-mañjarī in the western part of Citrā-devī's grove, and in gaura-līlā she appears as Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, known as the bhāgavata-ācārya.
body: Rasānandada-kuñja is the kuñja of Rasa-mañjarī in the western part of Citrā-devī's grove, and in gaura-līlā she appears as Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, known as the bhāgavata-ācārya. Her eternal form is that of a thirteen-year-old girl dressed in white, and she is very dear to Rūpa-mañjarī. Tradition describes her companion Vilāsa-mañjarī collecting bath water from the Yamunā in golden jugs.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rati-kuṇḍa
summary: Rati-kuṇḍa, also called Ratu, lies further along traditional walk.
body: Rati-kuṇḍa, also called Ratu, lies further along traditional walk. In a nearby grove Kṛṣṇa and Rādhārāṇī acted as puppets in the hands of Cupid, displaying Their romantic mastery in pastimes of transcendental passion (rati). The amorous love of this material world has its original, pure form in Vraja, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are the prototypes for all youthful lovers.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Ratna-kuṇḍa
summary: Ratna-kuṇḍa is a lake near the dancing arena in Kadamba-khaṇḍī, named because its waters abound with the jewels of ecstatic love that true saints see and touch.
body: Ratna-kuṇḍa is a lake near the dancing arena in Kadamba-khaṇḍī, named because its waters abound with the jewels of ecstatic love that true saints see and touch. It lies just behind Ratna-siṁhāsana, the throne of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Śyāmavana, and beside it is a rāsa-vedī where Kṛṣṇa danced with the gopīs. The account also gives Ratna-kuṇḍa's alternate name as Muktā-kuṇḍa, north of Dabharāro, where the gopīs refused Kṛṣṇa's request for pearl necklaces to decorate His cows for Dīpāvalī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Ratyambuja-kuñja
summary: Ratyambuja-kuñja lies in the southern part of Indulekhā-gopī's grove, where the mild-mannered Rati-mañjarī resides.
body: Ratyambuja-kuñja lies in the southern part of Indulekhā-gopī's grove, where the mild-mannered Rati-mañjarī resides. She is known as Tulasī-mañjarī in Vraja and as Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī in the pastimes of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Tradition quotes Raghunātha's lament, after Rūpa Gosvāmī's passing, that Rādhā-kuṇḍa had become like the gaping jaws of a tiger.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Ravar-kuṇḍa
summary: On the banks of Ravar-kuṇḍa, Viśākhā and her friends made statues of Kṛṣṇa from mud and decorated them with flowers and twigs.
body: On the banks of Ravar-kuṇḍa, Viśākhā and her friends made statues of Kṛṣṇa from mud and decorated them with flowers and twigs. Today a temple of Gopāla and a temple of Daujī stand at that site. Tradition quotes a prayer to Viśākhā to protect Rādhā's life, which is afflicted by separation from Kṛṣṇa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Raṅga-sthala
summary: Raṅga-sthala is the boys' wrestling arena, located near the stakes where Kṛṣṇa tamed the calves.
body: Raṅga-sthala is the boys' wrestling arena, located near the stakes where Kṛṣṇa tamed the calves. Kṛṣṇa visits it almost as religiously as the milking barns, but only after milking is complete. Some gopas take the part of contestants while others watch and cheer for their chosen heroes, and the place is also listed among the twenty-four tīrthas of Mathurā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Raṅgadevī-sukhaprada-kuñja
summary: This grove lies in the southwestern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa and gives unlimited happiness to its stewardess, Raṅgadevī, which is the source of its name.
body: This grove lies in the southwestern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa and gives unlimited happiness to its stewardess, Raṅgadevī, which is the source of its name. Everything in it is blackish, from the tamāla trees entwined by black vines to the ground and pavilions covered with sapphires. Rādhikā's attraction to Her lover grows whenever She comes here, because whatever She sees reminds Her of Śyāma.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Revatī-kuṇḍa
summary: Revatī-kuṇḍa is one of the lakes of Dakṣiṇā, a village also called Jakhīna after a witch (yakṣiṇī) whom Balarāma killed.
body: Revatī-kuṇḍa is one of the lakes of Dakṣiṇā, a village also called Jakhīna after a witch (yakṣiṇī) whom Balarāma killed. Together with Balarāma-kuṇḍa, it honours Kṛṣṇa's elder brother and His consort. The account also cites Dakṣiṇā as one place where Kṛṣṇa tasted Rādhā's submission.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Reṇukā-kuṇḍa
summary: Reṇukā-kuṇḍa is one of the lakes of Dakṣiṇā, where Jamadagni-kuṇḍa marks the place the sage Jamadagni once resided.
body: Reṇukā-kuṇḍa is one of the lakes of Dakṣiṇā, where Jamadagni-kuṇḍa marks the place the sage Jamadagni once resided. The village of Dakṣiṇā is named Jakhīna after a witch whom Balarāma killed. Jamadagni serves as an example of how sincere seekers of the Absolute Truth find Him as a transcendental cowherd boy who resides far beyond Vaikuṇṭha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rudan-kuṇḍa
summary: Rudan-kuṇḍa, also called Rudra-kuṇḍa, formed from the tears of compassion that Lord Śiva shed on the ground while praying to the divine couple to give pure devotion to wayward souls.
body: Rudan-kuṇḍa, also called Rudra-kuṇḍa, formed from the tears of compassion that Lord Śiva shed on the ground while praying to the divine couple to give pure devotion to wayward souls. It is named for the crying (rudan) of Rudra, who was its source, and bathing there is said to bring the mercy of the universal father. People who receive Śiva's mercy are no longer drawn to karma, jñāna, yoga, or mukti.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rudra-kuṇḍa
summary: Rudra-kuṇḍa lies in the centre of the larger Harajī-kuṇḍa in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, named for the gopa Hara, who played ball with Kṛṣṇa nearby, and Vaiṣṇavas visit it to honour Lord Śiva as the best of devotees.
body: Rudra-kuṇḍa lies in the centre of the larger Harajī-kuṇḍa in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, named for the gopa Hara, who played ball with Kṛṣṇa nearby, and Vaiṣṇavas visit it to honour Lord Śiva as the best of devotees. Its deep, clear water made it a favourite of Kṛṣṇa, His cowherd friends, and the gopīs, and Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā bathed and swam there, though Kṛṣṇa once left Rādhā, a weak swimmer, in the middle of the lake. Its pastimes are remembered as sad, recounting how the gopīs' weeping overflowed the lake when they learned Kṛṣṇa had gone to the Yamunā, and how the Vraja-vāsīs wept on its shore when Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma passed on their way to Mathurā. The lake is made doubly effective by the tears shed by Lord Śiva, granting loving devotion to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rudra-sarovara
summary: Rudra-sarovara is one of the lakes named in a verse from the Vraja-vilāsa-stava that glorifies the beautiful lakes encircling Govardhana Hill like jewels.
body: Rudra-sarovara is one of the lakes named in a verse from the Vraja-vilāsa-stava that glorifies the beautiful lakes encircling Govardhana Hill like jewels. The verse lists it alongside Śrī-sarovara, Brahma-sarovara, Kadamba-khaṇḍa-sarovara, and others. Tradition offers this verse as a way to glorify these transcendental lakes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rudravana
summary: Rudravana is the forest where Rudra-kuṇḍa is nestled among the trees along the route through Girirāja's orchards.
body: Rudravana is the forest where Rudra-kuṇḍa is nestled among the trees along the route through Girirāja's orchards. Kṛṣṇa would sneak away from the cows and cowherd boys resting at Go-kuṇḍa in Śyāma-ḍhāk to meet Rādhā and a few intimate companions here. It was also here that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa changed into bathing clothes to refresh themselves in the lotus-filled water of Rudra-kuṇḍa during the midday heat.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Runakī-kuṇḍa
summary: Runakī-kuṇḍa and Jhunakī-kuṇḍa are two hidden lakes in Domīlavana, the forest where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa meet (milana) on the way around Nandagrāma.
body: Runakī-kuṇḍa and Jhunakī-kuṇḍa are two hidden lakes in Domīlavana, the forest where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa meet (milana) on the way around Nandagrāma. The forest is also called Domanavana, because the minds (mana) of the divine couple merge there. The two lakes and the groves around them are named for two gopīs who arranged for the couple to meet there.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rādhā-saubhāgya-mandira
summary: Rādhā-saubhāgya-mandira is one of the eight names of the Yoga-pīṭha, meaning the auspicious temple of Rādhā.
body: Rādhā-saubhāgya-mandira is one of the eight names of the Yoga-pīṭha, meaning the auspicious temple of Rādhā. Mahādeva promises that calling the eight names with affection upon waking will attract Govindajī and bring love for Kṛṣṇa. Devotees are advised to recite them as one would the Gopāla mantra and meditating always on Śrī Govinda.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rādhāvana
summary: Rādhāvana is the area north of Abhirāma Ṭhākura's samādhi, bounded by Gauravana and Aṭalavana and reaching the Yamunā up to Jagannātha-ghāṭa, and it is named after Rādhā, who is as fond of it as of Her lake.
body: Rādhāvana is the area north of Abhirāma Ṭhākura's samādhi, bounded by Gauravana and Aṭalavana and reaching the Yamunā up to Jagannātha-ghāṭa, and it is named after Rādhā, who is as fond of it as of Her lake. Devotional accounts describe gopīs such as Lalitā and Viśākhā braiding Śrī Rādhā's hair after bathing in the Yamunā, decorated with fragrant forest flowers. In one pastime Vṛndā dressed Kṛṣṇa as a gopī, and Rādhā was enchanted by Him without recognising Him. Tradition mentions four samādhis here, of Govindānanda, Mādhava Ghoṣa, Vāsudeva Ghoṣa, and Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita, and a shoreline of weeping willows where Kṛṣṇa played hide-and-seek with Rādhā and Her friends.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rāja-ghāṭa
summary: Rāja-ghāṭa is a landing at the centre of Papaḍavana on the Yamunā, where boats once ferried people across the river.
body: Rāja-ghāṭa is a landing at the centre of Papaḍavana on the Yamunā, where boats once ferried people across the river. Kṛṣṇa disguised Himself as a boatman here, and when Rādhārāṇī and Her friends, carrying milk products to relatives in Rāval and Gokula, threatened to report the lazy boatman to the king (rāja), Kṛṣṇa revealed His identity and immersed them in bliss, which is why the landing is so named. A stately banyan tree stands here, under which Caitanya Mahāprabhu rested on His way to Akrūra-ghāṭa and Keśī-tīrtha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rāma-kuṇḍa
summary: Rāma-kuṇḍa is a lake in the northwest corner of Pāvana-sarovara at Nandagrāma.
body: Rāma-kuṇḍa is a lake in the northwest corner of Pāvana-sarovara at Nandagrāma. Rādhā's tower and summer kitchen were nearby, which made the lake a convenient place for part of Kṛṣṇa's birthday festival, and in summer Kṛṣṇa's morning meal was served on the banks of Pāvana-sarovara. Tradition describes sitting in the lake's pavilion to chant japa while surveying the pastime places of the dhāma. That after Kṛṣṇa killed Śaṅkhacūḍa at nearby Sāṅkhi, He gave the Syamantaka jewel to Balarāma at Rāma-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rāsa-kuṇḍa
summary: Rāsa-kuṇḍa is a lake at Rāsolī, near Raṅkolī, where Kṛṣṇa called the gopīs visiting their parents in Varṣāṇā with His flute and enjoyed rāsa dancing beneath a large banyan tree.
body: Rāsa-kuṇḍa is a lake at Rāsolī, near Raṅkolī, where Kṛṣṇa called the gopīs visiting their parents in Varṣāṇā with His flute and enjoyed rāsa dancing beneath a large banyan tree. Afterwards He encouraged the tired gopīs to refresh themselves in the lake, where they played water games, and then they enjoyed a picnic of luscious fruits catered by Vṛndā-devī. The demigods, who could not see through the tree's canopy from their airplanes, could only hear the rāsa dance.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rāsavedī-ghāṭa
summary: Rāsavedī-ghāṭa is the southern side of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, the place of the rāsa dance.
body: Rāsavedī-ghāṭa is the southern side of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, the place of the rāsa dance. Its two corners and its centre are decorated, in unmanifest forms, by the groves of Indulekhā, Raṅgadevī, and Campakalatā. Nearby, the ancient Imlī-talā tamarind tree is related to one of Rūpa Gosvāmī's wonderful pastimes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Rūpollāsa-kuñja
summary: Rūpollāsa-kuñja is the sub-grove of Rūpa-mañjarī, set in a corner of Lalitā-devī's grove and designated in New Vraja-dhāma as the front left portion of the temple room.
body: Rūpollāsa-kuñja is the sub-grove of Rūpa-mañjarī, set in a corner of Lalitā-devī's grove and designated in New Vraja-dhāma as the front left portion of the temple room. Devotional accounts describe Rūpa-mañjarī massaging Rādhā's feet during a game of dice, and cooling the exhausted youthful couple with a fan of blossoming vines. Next to it is Vilāsānandada-kuñja, where Vilāsa-mañjarī stays, and who in Caitanya's pastimes appears as Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sakhī-kuṇḍa
summary: Sakhī-kuṇḍa and Līlāvatī-kuṇḍa are lakes in the Sakhīvana woods past Govardhana town, near the village of Sakhī-sthalī.
body: Sakhī-kuṇḍa and Līlāvatī-kuṇḍa are lakes in the Sakhīvana woods past Govardhana town, near the village of Sakhī-sthalī. Govardhana Malla, a revenue collector for Kaṁsa and close friend of Rādhā's husband Abhimanyu, lives there with his wife Candrāvalī. Devotional accounts describe Candrāvalī, whom scripture declares to be Kṛṣṇa's second-favourite gopī, as Rādhā's competitor in a special sense.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sakhīvana
summary: Sakhīvana is a woodland beside the parikrama path just past Govardhana town, reputed for its large-leafed palāśa trees.
body: Sakhīvana is a woodland beside the parikrama path just past Govardhana town, reputed for its large-leafed palāśa trees. Uddhava spoke of Kṛṣṇa to the gopīs here, and they rode the waves of their ecstatic bliss as driftwood is tossed about by the sea. Tradition describes King Vajranābha standing guard around Puṣpavana and Sakhīvana during a kīrtana festival, and Parīkṣit Mahārāja singing and dancing with the queens as they circled Sakhīvana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
