title: Salila-kamala-kuñja
summary: Salila-kamala-kuñja is the secret island grove of Anaṅga-mañjarī at the centre of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, connected to the northern ghāṭa by a bridge.
body: Salila-kamala-kuñja is the secret island grove of Anaṅga-mañjarī at the centre of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, connected to the northern ghāṭa by a bridge. Designed as a sixteen-petalled lotus floating on the water and covered with emeralds, rubies, and moonstones, it has swans and lilies that appear to bob with the waves. A golden cottage inlaid with moonstones stands at its centre.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Samādhivana
summary: Samādhivana is the eastern corner of Khoṅha, the gopīs' playing field where Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Her friends played kho-kho, opposite Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī's samādhi.
body: Samādhivana is the eastern corner of Khoṅha, the gopīs' playing field where Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Her friends played kho-kho, opposite Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī's samādhi. It holds the samādhis of the sixty-four primary associates of Lord Caitanya, many of which are nāma-samādhis. Jīva Gosvāmī brought some of Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī's ashes from Rādhā-kuṇḍa and built a second samādhi for Raghunātha here.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sandarśana-kuṇḍa
summary: Sandarśana-kuṇḍa is one of the fifty-six lakes that the ācāryas singled out as most prominent in Vraja, although the lakes themselves cannot be counted.
body: Sandarśana-kuṇḍa is one of the fifty-six lakes that the ācāryas singled out as most prominent in Vraja, although the lakes themselves cannot be counted. Scripture says all the holy lakes of the universe take shelter in Vṛndāvana during the month of Kārttika. Tradition names Sandarśana-kuṇḍa among the lakes mentioned for his own purification, and no pastime is described for it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sannihita-sarovara
summary: Sannihita-sarovara is a smaller kuṇḍa near the lake that King Kuru excavated at Kurukṣetra, and pilgrims offer oblations for departed souls there.
body: Sannihita-sarovara is a smaller kuṇḍa near the lake that King Kuru excavated at Kurukṣetra, and pilgrims offer oblations for departed souls there. It was also the secluded area where Kṛṣṇa met with the Vraja-vāsīs. There are many other pastime places throughout Kurukṣetra and the nearby area.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sapta-sāmudrika-kuṇḍa
summary: Sapta-sāmudrika-kuṇḍa was a clear-water lake that once existed where the well called Kṛṣṇa-kūpa, Nanda-kūpa, or Sapta-sāmudrika-kūpa now stands, east of Sanātana Gosvāmī's cave.
body: Sapta-sāmudrika-kuṇḍa was a clear-water lake that once existed where the well called Kṛṣṇa-kūpa, Nanda-kūpa, or Sapta-sāmudrika-kūpa now stands, east of Sanātana Gosvāmī's cave. The well marks the place of Kṛṣṇa's ear-piercing ceremony, and the account suggests it may have been a lake in the past. Scripture says that offering piṇḍa to ancestors at this lake on the Monday after the new moon equals performing that rite at holy Gayā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saptarṣi-ghāṭa
summary: Saptarṣi-ghāṭa lies next to the place where Dhruva attained perfection, and it is where the seven sages Marīci, Atri, Aṅgirā, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha performed austerities.
body: Saptarṣi-ghāṭa lies next to the place where Dhruva attained perfection, and it is where the seven sages Marīci, Atri, Aṅgirā, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha performed austerities. Their deities, about five thousand years old, are still worshipped there. Pilgrims who visit gain access either to these sages' planets or to transcendental devotion, depending on their desire.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sarasvatī-kuṇḍa
summary: Sarasvatī-kuṇḍa is where Balarāma accompanied the Vraja-vāsīs as far as the lake, while Kṛṣṇa hurried on to Vasudeva's house, His new home in Mathurā.
body: Sarasvatī-kuṇḍa is where Balarāma accompanied the Vraja-vāsīs as far as the lake, while Kṛṣṇa hurried on to Vasudeva's house, His new home in Mathurā. There Nanda Mahārāja, speaking with great difficulty, asked his elder son to follow His brother and never let Him out of sight, as their mother had often said.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sarasvatī-tīrtha
summary: Sarasvatī-tīrtha is the confluence of the Sarasvatī and Yamunā rivers, where merely touching the water is said to bless one with the detachment of the renounced order (sannyāsa).
body: Sarasvatī-tīrtha is the confluence of the Sarasvatī and Yamunā rivers, where merely touching the water is said to bless one with the detachment of the renounced order (sannyāsa). In New Vraja-dhāma it lies between Vighnarāja-ghāṭa and Gokarṇa-ghāṭa, a different location from its position in Bhauma Vṛndāvana. No pastime is told about this tīrtha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sarvabhāvana
summary: Sarvabhāvana appears in traditional accounts only in the bibliography, where it is the name of the translator of Śrī Caitanya Candrāmṛtaṁ.
body: Sarvabhāvana appears in traditional accounts only in the bibliography, where it is the name of the translator of Śrī Caitanya Candrāmṛtaṁ. It is not described as a place.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Satohā-grāma
summary: Satohā-grāma is where Kīrtidā sent Rādhā, with her grandmother Mukharā, into hiding to escape King Kaṁsa's plan to marry her.
body: Satohā-grāma is where Kīrtidā sent Rādhā, with her grandmother Mukharā, into hiding to escape King Kaṁsa's plan to marry her. On Paurṇamāsī's advice, Rādhā was married to Abhimanyu, son of Mukharā's friend Jaṭilā, at Satohā-grāma, which would keep Kaṁsa from pursuing her and reduce his envy of Kṛṣṇa. Soon after the wedding Rādhā moved with Abhimanyu to Yāvaṭā, where she accepted Kṛṣṇa as her paramour. Mother Yaśodā laments the loss of such a daughter-in-law.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṁyamana-tīrtha
summary: Saṁyamana-tīrtha, also called Svāmī-ghāṭa, is famous for subduing the power of Yamarāja and bestowing liberation.
body: Saṁyamana-tīrtha, also called Svāmī-ghāṭa, is famous for subduing the power of Yamarāja and bestowing liberation. Kṛṣṇa bathed here while pacifying the Yadus and performing rites for His dead uncle, after first bathing at Viśrāma-ghāṭa. Devotional accounts tell of a hunter who drowned trying to cross the Yamunā at this tīrtha and was reborn as a king of the Saurāṣṭra country through its power. The account also describes Dhārāpatana-tīrtha, at the foot of Kaṁsa-ṭīlā, as lying just before it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṅgama-kuñja
summary: Saṅgama-kuñja is the place where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa met (saṅgama) to relish each other's company, and it adjoins Saṅgama-kuṇḍa.
body: Saṅgama-kuñja is the place where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa met (saṅgama) to relish each other's company, and it adjoins Saṅgama-kuṇḍa. When Caitanya Mahāprabhu heard that the couple's amorous pastimes here concluded with the rāsa dance, He joyfully exclaimed, “Excellent!” Lokanātha Gosvāmī performed bhajana here, sometimes in the company of his friend Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṅgama-kuṇḍa
summary: Saṅgama-kuṇḍa is a favourite lake of the gopas and gopīs, adjoining Saṅgama-kuñja, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa met to enjoy each other's company.
body: Saṅgama-kuṇḍa is a favourite lake of the gopas and gopīs, adjoining Saṅgama-kuñja, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa met to enjoy each other's company. Date trees grow profusely nearby, so hungry cowherd boys come to collect dates and play in the lake, filling the forest with their laughter. The couple's amorous pastimes here concluded with the rāsa dance, which Caitanya Mahāprabhu greeted with joy.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa
summary: Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa lies in Bahulāvana beside Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa, and tradition says that bathing in these lakes during the month of Caitra lets one see the forms of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa who reside in the forest.
body: Saṅkarṣaṇa-kuṇḍa lies in Bahulāvana beside Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa, and tradition says that bathing in these lakes during the month of Caitra lets one see the forms of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa who reside in the forest. The lake is also Baladeva's pastime place, where Balarāma and the cowherd boys tended the cows around Nai, resting on its banks while Kṛṣṇa met the gopīs elsewhere. In one pastime, after the summer rains had receded, Kṛṣṇa strolled alone along the banks in a mood of romantic adventure. The lake is also named among the holy places around Parāsaulī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṅketa-kuñja
summary: Saṅketa-kuñja is a grove at Saṅketa where Kṛṣṇa brought Rādhārāṇī after the rāsa dance to decorate her lovingly with flowers, and other Gosvāmīs visited to see it.
body: Saṅketa-kuñja is a grove at Saṅketa where Kṛṣṇa brought Rādhārāṇī after the rāsa dance to decorate her lovingly with flowers, and other Gosvāmīs visited to see it. Behind the temple of Saṅketa-devī is a rāsa-vedī commemorating the rāsa-līlā here, and nearby a tree on which the gopīs swing the divine couple. Tradition recounts how Kṛṣṇa paced the courtyard, worried that Jaṭilā had locked Rādhā up when she failed to arrive at their appointed time, before setting out with Madhumaṅgala toward Varṣāṇā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṅketavana
summary: Saṅketavana is a dense forest midway between Nandagrāma and Varṣāṇā, grown from the fertile soil of the divine couple's meetings (saṅketa).
body: Saṅketavana is a dense forest midway between Nandagrāma and Varṣāṇā, grown from the fertile soil of the divine couple's meetings (saṅketa). Its trees, vines, flowers, and creepers correspond to the four types of meetings (sambhoga) between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. The name also denotes a meeting place set up by mirror signals that Rādhārāṇī and Kṛṣṇa sent from their respective bedrooms in Varṣāṇā and Nandagrāma.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Saṅketavaṭa
summary: Saṅketavaṭa is the first of the sixteen banyan trees listed in traditional accounts on pastime places on the parikrama.
body: Saṅketavaṭa is the first of the sixteen banyan trees listed in traditional accounts on pastime places on the parikrama. Devotional accounts give its name only in that list and describe no pastime for it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sei-kuṇḍa
summary: At Sei, Brahmā saw Kṛṣṇa in the cows and calves and finally understood that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord, repeating “ei sei, ei sei” (“He is that!
body: At Sei, Brahmā saw Kṛṣṇa in the cows and calves and finally understood that Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord, repeating “ei sei, ei sei” (“He is that! He is that!”). Sei-kuṇḍa and the temple of Vatsa-bihārī are here, along with a pippala tree worshipped as the four-headed Brahmā. A deity of Brahmā in a grove outside the village replaces an original that was sadly stolen.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Setubandha-kuṇḍa
summary: Setubandha-kuṇḍa, also called Laṅkā-kuṇḍa, represents the point of the ocean at Rameśvara from which Lord Rāmacandra crossed to Laṅkā over a bridge of joined boulders.
body: Setubandha-kuṇḍa, also called Laṅkā-kuṇḍa, represents the point of the ocean at Rameśvara from which Lord Rāmacandra crossed to Laṅkā over a bridge of joined boulders. Devotional accounts describe Kṛṣṇa sitting by this lake one summer day with Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Her friends, watching monkeys leap from the trees into the water. That Kāman was originally walled, with seven gates, one of them in the direction of Setubandha-kuṇḍa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Setubhanda-kuṇḍa
summary: Setubhanda-kuṇḍa is a lake in Kāmyavana, where Kṛṣṇa showed the gopīs His pastime of building a stone bridge to cross to Laṅkā, as described in the account on Kāmyavana.
body: Setubhanda-kuṇḍa is a lake in Kāmyavana, where Kṛṣṇa showed the gopīs His pastime of building a stone bridge to cross to Laṅkā, as described in the account on Kāmyavana. The account is otherwise a prayer by Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura glorifying Govinda.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sitāmbuja-kuñja
summary: Sitāmbuja-kuñja is the all-white grove lying to the north in the lotus arrangement of groves, made of nāga-kesara and punnāga trees and every variety of jasmine vine heavy with tiny white blossoms.
body: Sitāmbuja-kuñja is the all-white grove lying to the north in the lotus arrangement of groves, made of nāga-kesara and punnāga trees and every variety of jasmine vine heavy with tiny white blossoms. Its lotus whorl is fashioned from gold-studded moonstones and its filaments from artistically set pearls. Tradition describes the nearby Mādhavānandada-kuñja, where Lalitā stores and offers gifts of love to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Soma-tīrtha
summary: Soma-tīrtha lies downstream from Cakra-tīrtha, where those who follow the rules of their varṇa and āśrama may gain access to the moon planet (soma) by bathing.
body: Soma-tīrtha lies downstream from Cakra-tīrtha, where those who follow the rules of their varṇa and āśrama may gain access to the moon planet (soma) by bathing. It is also called Kṛṣṇa-gaṅgā-ghāṭa, because Kṛṣṇa made the Ganges appear in the middle of the Yamunā here. Bathing here is ten times more auspicious than the world's five most sacred baths.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Soṅkh-kuṇḍa
summary: Soṅkh is the clearing where Rādhikā's spicing attracted two friends, the gopīs fed them, and Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā retired to a kuñja after eating.
body: Soṅkh is the clearing where Rādhikā's spicing attracted two friends, the gopīs fed them, and Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā retired to a kuñja after eating. Soṅkh-kuṇḍa is one of several lakes and temples in this area, and it is said that the aroma of the gopīs' cooking can still be smelled here. The parikrama path turns from here toward Kāmyavana along a line of trees separating the two valleys.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Subalānandada-kuñja
summary: A grove on the northwestern side of Śyāma-kuṇḍa that belongs to Subala, the cowherd friend of Kṛṣṇa.
body: A grove on the northwestern side of Śyāma-kuṇḍa that belongs to Subala, the cowherd friend of Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Rādhā accepts it as Her own, so it is the foremost of the groves surrounding Śyāma’s lake. Rādhā first bathed in Śyāma-kuṇḍa at the foot of this grove, and ever since She and Her girlfriends have come there at noon each day to bathe at the ghāṭa called Mānasa-pāvana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sudarśana-kuṇḍa
summary: The place where Kṛṣṇa saved Nanda Mahārāja and liberated the celestial Sudarśana, who had been a snake and was freed of his sinful body by the touch of Kṛṣṇa’s foot.
body: The place where Kṛṣṇa saved Nanda Mahārāja and liberated the celestial Sudarśana, who had been a snake and was freed of his sinful body by the touch of Kṛṣṇa’s foot. Bathing here frees one from all sin and qualifies one to be touched by the Lord’s lotus feet. The next morning the Vraja-vāsīs left for Nandagrāma praising Kṛṣṇa for saving His father and liberating Sudarśana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sudevī-sukhada-kuñja
summary: The emerald grove of Sudevī, located in the northwestern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, where the vines, trees, birds and bees are all green and the pavilions are studded with emeralds.
body: The emerald grove of Sudevī, located in the northwestern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, where the vines, trees, birds and bees are all green and the pavilions are studded with emeralds. Within a cottage on one of its platforms, Rādhā with Her friends and Kṛṣṇa with His friends play games of dice. Madhumaṅgala is Kṛṣṇa’s advisor and Lalitā is Rādhā’s, and Sudevī is especially good at the dice game of pāśa-khela, which she hosts in her grove.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sumanaḥ-sarovara
summary: Also called Kusuma-sarovara, a beautiful lake at the centre of Puṣpavana, whose banks echo with birds and bees.
body: Also called Kusuma-sarovara, a beautiful lake at the centre of Puṣpavana, whose banks echo with birds and bees. After rediscovering Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa, Caitanya Mahāprabhu came here and saw Govardhana Hill for the first time, and He paid obeisances to it. Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī uses the name Sumanaḥ-sarovara in Caitanya-caritāmṛta, and tradition notes that Śrī Uddhava recited Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam at this lake.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Surabhi-kuñja
summary: A grove in Godrumadvīpa where Ṭhākura Bhaktivinoda would later build his home.
body: A grove in Godrumadvīpa where Ṭhākura Bhaktivinoda would later build his home. Indra and Surabhi came here after Surabhi advised them to worship Caitanya Mahāprabhu in Navadvīpa, and they chanted the name Gaurāṅga incessantly. Quickly attaining the vision of Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Indra was addressed by the Lord with compassion and a voice choked with love.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sutala-kuṇḍa
summary: A small lake in the dense groves of Sutalavana, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa would rest after enjoying a rāsa dance.
body: A small lake in the dense groves of Sutalavana, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa would rest after enjoying a rāsa dance. The famous cave of Maṇikandalī is only a short distance away. The account also notes that this area lies along the parikrama path where it bends around Girirāja’s southern side.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sutalavana
summary: A small forest enclosed by the parikrama path where it bends around Girirāja’s southern side, with Śyāma-ḍhāk forest on the opposite side of the path.
body: A small forest enclosed by the parikrama path where it bends around Girirāja’s southern side, with Śyāma-ḍhāk forest on the opposite side of the path. Sutala-kuṇḍa is in its groves. It was near Samāi, at the bend around Sutalavana, that Lauṭhā, the gopa friend who is also known as Lauṭhā Bābā and is regarded as an expansion of Hanumān, waved goodbye to Kṛṣṇa as Akrūra’s chariot left. The account also describes a later return of Kṛṣṇa to Vṛndāvana, when He took the Vraja-vāsīs back to Goloka.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Svāmī-ghāṭa
summary: Also called Saṁyamana-tīrtha, a bathing place on the Yamunā in Mathurā, famous for subduing the power of Yamarāja and bestowing the perfection of liberation.
body: Also called Saṁyamana-tīrtha, a bathing place on the Yamunā in Mathurā, famous for subduing the power of Yamarāja and bestowing the perfection of liberation. After killing Kaṁsa, Kṛṣṇa first bathed at Viśrāma-ghāṭa and later bathed here while pacifying the Yadus and performing the rituals for His dead uncle. The ghāṭa is located after Dhārāpatana-tīrtha, at the foot of Kaṁsa-ṭīlā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja
summary: A lotus-shaped island grove at the centre of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, belonging to Anaṅga-mañjarī, the manifestation of Balarāma who serves Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the mellow of amorous love.
body: A lotus-shaped island grove at the centre of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, belonging to Anaṅga-mañjarī, the manifestation of Balarāma who serves Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the mellow of amorous love. From this grove she arranges the divine couple’s midday pastimes. This grove is physically connected to Lalitā-devī’s grove, and Kamalā-mañjarī has a grove of the same name.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sābalā-grāma
summary: A village in the Kāmyavana area of Bhauma Vṛndāvana, toward which tradition walked through a peaceful stretch of land.
body: A village in the Kāmyavana area of Bhauma Vṛndāvana, toward which tradition walked through a peaceful stretch of land. In Kṛṣṇa’s time the encroaching desert had dried up the lakes in this area, so trees grew only in the damp lakebeds. The cowherd boys found it difficult to water their cows or bathe when they passed this way.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sāhasī-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake in a banyan forest facing Nandagrāma, also called Sārasi-kuṇḍa, further from the road than Leovaṭa-kuṇḍa.
body: A lake in a banyan forest facing Nandagrāma, also called Sārasi-kuṇḍa, further from the road than Leovaṭa-kuṇḍa. Its name comes from sāhasī, meaning determined, which reflects the determination of the young gopīs to bring Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa together even so close to His home. The gopīs once brought Rādhā here, where Kṛṣṇa was waiting, and seated the divine couple on a decorated swing while they sang of His heroic pastimes. Mother Yaśodā could hear their saṅkīrtana from Nanda-bhavana.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sārasi-kuṇḍa
summary: Another name for Sāhasī-kuṇḍa, meaning Swan Lake.
body: Another name for Sāhasī-kuṇḍa, meaning Swan Lake. Mother Yaśodā, unable to see her boys who were playing around the lake, called Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma the swans (sārasa) of her life, one black and one white, and the boys then decided to call the lake Sārasi-kuṇḍa. Both names have been used ever since. Behind the grove of banyan trees lies a fertile field called Muktā-tīrtha, where Kṛṣṇa watered His cows at a clear lake in the centre.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sūrya-ghāṭa
summary: A bathing place on the Yamunā where the sun god, Sūrya-nārāyaṇa, performed austerities so that he might directly see and serve Kṛṣṇa, and where he was eventually given assurance that his desire would be fulfilled.
body: A bathing place on the Yamunā where the sun god, Sūrya-nārāyaṇa, performed austerities so that he might directly see and serve Kṛṣṇa, and where he was eventually given assurance that his desire would be fulfilled. The sun god appeared in person to Sāmba, freeing him from leprosy and letting him ride on the chariot of the sun. Inland from this ghāṭa is Bali-ṭīlā, where Bali Mahārāja performed the Viśvajit sacrifice. Rādhā once also set out toward this ghāṭa to worship the sun god.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Sūrya-tīrtha
summary: A bathing place in Mathurā that destroys all sin, where Bali Mahārāja long ago pleased the sun god and received a cintāmaṇi gem and blessings to conquer the universe.
body: A bathing place in Mathurā that destroys all sin, where Bali Mahārāja long ago pleased the sun god and received a cintāmaṇi gem and blessings to conquer the universe. Bathing here during a solar or lunar eclipse yields more benefit than a Rājasūya sacrifice. Sāmba, cursed with leprosy, followed Nārada’s instructions to worship the sun here morning, noon and evening, and then bathe in the Kṛṣṇa-gaṅgā.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tamālavana
summary: A part of the Vṛndāvana forest just outside Vṛndāvana village, sloping gently toward the Yamunā valley and dominated by the secluded gardens Śyāmabagh and Rāmabagh, named after Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.
body: A part of the Vṛndāvana forest just outside Vṛndāvana village, sloping gently toward the Yamunā valley and dominated by the secluded gardens Śyāmabagh and Rāmabagh, named after Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. The hill that slopes down to Tamālavana is named Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa-ṭīlā after the lake Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa in one of its gardens. Devotional accounts mention that the administrative offices of New Vraja-dhāma are at its centre, and invites devotees to go to Kṛṣṇa-kuṇḍa-ṭīlā, sit in Holīvana, and chant the holy names.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tapovana
summary: A secluded forest valley among hills where Nara-Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi performs austerities even today.
body: A secluded forest valley among hills where Nara-Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi performs austerities even today. When King Indra sent Cupid and beautiful damsels to disturb the Lord’s meditation, the Lord calmly and politely welcomed them, and Cupid and his companions trembled in fear. The gopīs performed their worship of Kātyāyanī here, and the place is named Tapovana for the severe austerities they performed, and the sun god warmed their cold bodies.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tapta-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake some distance above Gaurī-kuṇḍa on the route to Ādi-badrī, which the account describes as not hot, despite its name, but still more purifying than its Himalayan counterpart.
body: A lake some distance above Gaurī-kuṇḍa on the route to Ādi-badrī, which the account describes as not hot, despite its name, but still more purifying than its Himalayan counterpart. Above this lake, on a large slab of black granite, sits a large Deity of Lord Badarīnātha in the posture of a yogī in meditation. The account also notes that Tapta means hot.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tarasa-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake formerly known as Toṣa-kuṇḍa, near Gandheśvara, where the cows drank water while the gopa Toṣa tutored Kṛṣṇa in dancing under large mango trees.
body: A lake formerly known as Toṣa-kuṇḍa, near Gandheśvara, where the cows drank water while the gopa Toṣa tutored Kṛṣṇa in dancing under large mango trees. Toṣa means satisfaction, and tradition notes that Toṣa satisfied Kṛṣṇa by his service. In Kṛṣṇa Valley the children’s gurukula school stands in this area.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Taḍāga-tīrtha
summary: A forest northeast of Pāvana-sarovara, where Parjanya Mahārāja, Kṛṣṇa’s grandfather, gave up eating and drinking on Nārada’s advice and performed penance to obtain a worthy descendant, until a voice from heaven promised five sons, the best of whom would be Nanda.
body: A forest northeast of Pāvana-sarovara, where Parjanya Mahārāja, Kṛṣṇa’s grandfather, gave up eating and drinking on Nārada’s advice and performed penance to obtain a worthy descendant, until a voice from heaven promised five sons, the best of whom would be Nanda. Sanātana Gosvāmī also performed bhajana here. The kadamba forest on the western side of the lake, where Taḍāga-tīrtha is found, is a favourite of Balarāma, who joins His friends here in games like hide-and-seek.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tinduka-tīrtha
summary: A sacred bathing place on the Yamunā in Mathurā, just downstream from Kaṅkhala-ghāṭa, where a destitute barber named Tinduka regularly bathed and was reborn as an aristocratic brāhmaṇa after leaving his body.
body: A sacred bathing place on the Yamunā in Mathurā, just downstream from Kaṅkhala-ghāṭa, where a destitute barber named Tinduka regularly bathed and was reborn as an aristocratic brāhmaṇa after leaving his body. It is adjoined by Daṇḍi-ghāṭa, named after Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who bathed there as a daṇḍī sannyāsī and which is also called Bengali-ghāṭa. The next bathing place is Sūrya-tīrtha.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Toṣa-kuṇḍa
summary: The former name of the lake now known as Tarasa-kuṇḍa, near Gandheśvara.
body: The former name of the lake now known as Tarasa-kuṇḍa, near Gandheśvara. It is named after the gopa Toṣa, one of Kṛṣṇa’s confidential friends, who was an accomplished dancer and helped Kṛṣṇa hone His dancing skills while the cows drank from the lake. Toṣa means satisfaction, and Toṣa satisfied Kṛṣṇa through his service.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tuṅgavidyānandada-kuñja
summary: The crimson grove of Tuṅgavidyā, located behind the western bathing ghāṭa of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, with reddish vines, trees, swings and flowers and platforms and pavilions set with rubies.
body: The crimson grove of Tuṅgavidyā, located behind the western bathing ghāṭa of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, with reddish vines, trees, swings and flowers and platforms and pavilions set with rubies. It is also known as Aruṇa-kuñja and is the delight of Rādhā’s dear girlfriend, and its ruddy brilliance ignites intense passionate love in the hearts of the divine couple. Next to it, in the northwestern corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, is the emerald grove of Sudevī.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Tṛṇāvarta-badha-sthala
summary: This place mainly in a note, which says it is also called Tṛṇāvarta-badha-sthala, meaning the place where Tṛṇāvarta was killed.
body: This place mainly in a note, which says it is also called Tṛṇāvarta-badha-sthala, meaning the place where Tṛṇāvarta was killed. The notes around it discuss the background of the demon, but the accounts give no further details of the pastime itself.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Udhā-grāma
summary: A village named because Uddhava stayed here on his way to the house of Nanda Mahārāja, as Rāghava Gosvāmī told Śrīnivāsa Ācārya and Ṭhākura Narottama.
body: A village named because Uddhava stayed here on his way to the house of Nanda Mahārāja, as Rāghava Gosvāmī told Śrīnivāsa Ācārya and Ṭhākura Narottama. Tired from his journey, Uddhava rested in the beauty and solitude of this forest garden and pondered the message Kṛṣṇa had asked him to give the Vraja-vāsīs. Uddhava’s mission was to pacify all the Vraja-vāsīs.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vajra-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake restored by Vajra after Kṛṣṇa left Vraja and the two lakes Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa had become simple ponds.
body: A lake restored by Vajra after Kṛṣṇa left Vraja and the two lakes Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa had become simple ponds. The lakes then became known as Kāñcana-kuṇḍa and Vajra-kuṇḍa. Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī later expanded Vajra-kuṇḍa into the present Śyāma-kuṇḍa, and the five sacred trees that were to be cut were allowed to remain after Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira appeared to him in a dream.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vallabha-ghāṭa
summary: A lakeshore on the western bank of Śyāma-kuṇḍa, reached by the path from the grove of Vidagdha and known to the followers of Vallabhācārya by this name, though it is also called Pāśa-khela-ghāṭa.
body: A lakeshore on the western bank of Śyāma-kuṇḍa, reached by the path from the grove of Vidagdha and known to the followers of Vallabhācārya by this name, though it is also called Pāśa-khela-ghāṭa. Pāśa-khela is a dice game requiring as much skill as luck, and Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa play it almost daily at Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Overwhelmed with joy on seeing Govardhana, Caitanya Mahāprabhu once embraced a stone from Girirāja on the path to Kusuma-sarovara.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Varāha-ghāṭa
summary: A landing on the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa revealed His boar incarnation to the curious cowherd girls, and where Gautama Muni had his āśrama.
body: A landing on the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa revealed His boar incarnation to the curious cowherd girls, and where Gautama Muni had his āśrama. From that time on, the landing has been known as Varāha-ghāṭa. It lies on the parikrama path where it turns onto the cowherd-boy trail, a short walk from ISKCON’s Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma temple, and its Varāha Deity was later stolen.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vasanta-sukhada-kuñja
summary: The northeast sub-petal of a lotus-shaped arrangement of groves around Rādhā-kuṇḍa, shaped like another eight-petalled lotus and filled with humming bees and singing cuckoos.
body: The northeast sub-petal of a lotus-shaped arrangement of groves around Rādhā-kuṇḍa, shaped like another eight-petalled lotus and filled with humming bees and singing cuckoos. It gives the spring season its joy, and it is one of the groves surrounding that eight-petalled arrangement.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vatsa-kuṇḍa
summary: Named in a passage describing Govardhana Hill as a living form, in which Vatsa-kuṇḍa is said to be the hill’s strength.
body: Named in a passage describing Govardhana Hill as a living form, in which Vatsa-kuṇḍa is said to be the hill’s strength. The passage also places Rudra-kuṇḍa as the hill’s anger and Śakra-sarovara as its desire. Faithfully hearing these descriptions removes all sins and makes one a qualified Vaiṣṇava.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vaṭasvāmī-tīrtha
summary: A bathing place in Mathurā dedicated to the worship of the sun god, which follows the sun god’s holy place at Bali-ṭīlā on the circuit.
body: A bathing place in Mathurā dedicated to the worship of the sun god, which follows the sun god’s holy place at Bali-ṭīlā on the circuit. Worshipping the sun god here on a Sunday brings good health, wealth and, at the end, the supreme destination. The Deity of the sun god worshipped here dates back to Satya-yuga.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Veda-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake in the Kāmyavana area, mentioned by the account mainly in a note, which lists it among other lakes there, including Dāmodara-kuṇḍa, Gandharva-kuṇḍa, Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa, Arghya-kuṇḍa and Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa.
body: A lake in the Kāmyavana area, mentioned by the account mainly in a note, which lists it among other lakes there, including Dāmodara-kuṇḍa, Gandharva-kuṇḍa, Nṛsiṁha-kuṇḍa, Arghya-kuṇḍa and Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa. No further pastime is told about it.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Veṇī-mādhava-ghāṭa
summary: The bathing place of the temple of Veṇī-mādhava, which Vajra established in the Mathurā area and which stands beside Prayāga-ghāṭa.
body: The bathing place of the temple of Veṇī-mādhava, which Vajra established in the Mathurā area and which stands beside Prayāga-ghāṭa. Further downstream is Kanakhala-tīrtha, a secret place that awards heavenly happiness, where Vajra installed a Deity of Rameśvara. The account also recounts that Lord Śiva saved the sage Pippalāyana from a demon at Prayāga-tīrtha and is worshipped there as Pippaleśvara.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vibudhāri-sarovara
summary: One of the many lakes glorified in a verse as shining in a circle around Govardhana Hill, like jewels, along with Śrī-sarovara, Brahma-sarovara, Sumanaḥ-sarovara and others.
body: One of the many lakes glorified in a verse as shining in a circle around Govardhana Hill, like jewels, along with Śrī-sarovara, Brahma-sarovara, Sumanaḥ-sarovara and others. It is mentioned mainly in this verse, which tradition uses to glorify these transcendental lakes.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vidrumavana
summary: A forest in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, named for the coral (vidruma) that paves the ground and the coral-coloured leaves of its trees.
body: A forest in Bhauma Vṛndāvana, named for the coral (vidruma) that paves the ground and the coral-coloured leaves of its trees. Tradition passed through it on the way to Baladeva, the first place reached, which is the pastime place of Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother Balarāma and is also called Daujī. Baladeva has a rich tradition of worshipping Balarāma’s Deity.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vidyādhara-kuṇḍa
summary: A lake on Śrī-śaila, which the account mentions in a verse praising Govardhana Hill.
body: A lake on Śrī-śaila, which the account mentions in a verse praising Govardhana Hill. The verse says that bathing daily for ten years in Vidyādhara-kuṇḍa on Śrī-śaila brings the result of a hundred yajñas, whereas one bath in Girirāja’s Pūñcāri-kuṇḍa is equal to ten million such results. It is mentioned only in this comparison.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vighnarāja-ghāṭa
summary: A bathing place on the Yamunā in Mathurā, also called Gaṇeśa-ghāṭa, which comes after Koṭi-ghāṭa.
body: A bathing place on the Yamunā in Mathurā, also called Gaṇeśa-ghāṭa, which comes after Koṭi-ghāṭa. There, by Lord Nṛsiṁha’s grace, Gaṇeśa removes all obstacles to pure devotion and bestows freedom from sins and miseries. It is a good place to scatter the ashes of departed souls into the Yamunā, so that the river carries them past all the tīrthas on her banks.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vighnarāja-tīrtha
summary: A place in Vraja where Kṛṣṇa appeared in the form of a Deity of Gaṇeśa, which the gopīs came to worship to remove any obstacle to their constant association with Kṛṣṇa, according to Vraja-rīti-cintāmaṇi.
body: A place in Vraja where Kṛṣṇa appeared in the form of a Deity of Gaṇeśa, which the gopīs came to worship to remove any obstacle to their constant association with Kṛṣṇa, according to Vraja-rīti-cintāmaṇi. The account also notes that this is one of three places where the gopīs bathed and had their clothes stolen by Kṛṣṇa.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vihvala-kuṇḍa
summary: A small pond formed by Kṛṣṇa’s tears, which flowed into a hollow beside the footpath after the Yogamāyā downpour overflowed His heart and eyes during His separation from Rādhā.
body: A small pond formed by Kṛṣṇa’s tears, which flowed into a hollow beside the footpath after the Yogamāyā downpour overflowed His heart and eyes during His separation from Rādhā. Its waters induce overwhelming feelings of separation in devotees who bathe in or drink from them. A four-armed form of Yogamāyā, Vihvala-devī, resides on the bank of the lake, though her temple is sorely neglected and falling into ruin.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vihāra-ghāṭa
summary: A pastime place on the Yamunā past Sūrya-ghāṭa, next to Yugala-ghāṭa, where the divine couple went after bathing to a nearby grove for their pleasures, decorating each other with flowers and eating fruit the gopīs had collected.
body: A pastime place on the Yamunā past Sūrya-ghāṭa, next to Yugala-ghāṭa, where the divine couple went after bathing to a nearby grove for their pleasures, decorating each other with flowers and eating fruit the gopīs had collected. After the rāsa dance, Kṛṣṇa searched the places dear to Rādhā, including Vihāra-ghāṭa, but could not find Her. Above Yugala-ghāṭa is the temple of Yugala-bihārī, where Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura and his followers once stayed.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vihāra-kuṇḍa
summary: Vihāra-kuṇḍa is a lake at the centre of Vihāravana, on whose bank Kṛṣṇa once sat playing His flute when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī was not present.
body: Vihāra-kuṇḍa is a lake at the centre of Vihāravana, on whose bank Kṛṣṇa once sat playing His flute when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī was not present. The gopīs were drawn to Him against their resistance, and when Rādhā saw His sapphire form in the sylvan setting her reluctance melted into the lake's waters. The lake stands beside Bāṅke-bihārī's temple in the forest.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vijñarāja-tīrtha
summary: Vijñarāja-tīrtha is mentioned mainly in passing as the point where the forest of Madhuvana begins along the bank of the Yamunā, extending to Bodhi-tīrtha and on to Tālavana.
body: Vijñarāja-tīrtha is mentioned mainly in passing as the point where the forest of Madhuvana begins along the bank of the Yamunā, extending to Bodhi-tīrtha and on to Tālavana. Madhuvana is identified with Kṛṣṇa, and tradition begins his parikrama of New Vraja-dhāma there. Little else is said about the place itself.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vilāsa-kuṇḍa
summary: Vilāsa-kuṇḍa is a lake in the flower garden beside Vilāsavana, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa cool off in its transparent waters.
body: Vilāsa-kuṇḍa is a lake in the flower garden beside Vilāsavana, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa cool off in its transparent waters. Devotional accounts recount how Kṛṣṇa, searching for Rādhā's lost ankle bell, braided a flower anklet and tied it on her foot there. Vaiṣṇavas say anklets with tiny golden bells can still be found on one bank, but only by those with unflinching faith. During Aurangzeb's reign, the Deity Harideva was immersed in this lake because its depth discouraged searchers.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vilāsavana
summary: Vilāsavana is a small, secluded forest on the parikrama path that is a special favourite of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa for their charming pastimes (vilāsa).
body: Vilāsavana is a small, secluded forest on the parikrama path that is a special favourite of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa for their charming pastimes (vilāsa). It is the scene of the lost-ankle-bell pastime, in which Rādhā dropped an ankle bell while collecting flowers and Kṛṣṇa found her searching and tied on a flower anklet. The couple then remained in the forest for intimate pastimes attended by one young girl, and the accounts say that all glories are offered to this forest.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vilāsānandada-kuñja
summary: Vilāsānandada-kuñja is a very beautiful grove next to Rūpollāsa-kuñja, within the grove of Viśākhā-devī.
body: Vilāsānandada-kuñja is a very beautiful grove next to Rūpollāsa-kuñja, within the grove of Viśākhā-devī. Vilāsa-mañjarī always stays there as one of the friends and followers of Śrī Rūpa. In Lord Caitanya's pastimes Vilāsa-mañjarī appears as Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, who systematised the philosophical conclusions of the Gauḍīya sampradāya.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Viśrāma-kuṇḍa
summary: Viśrāma-kuṇḍa lies just north of Dāvānala-kuṇḍa, near the terraced houses at the edge of Kevārivana.
body: Viśrāma-kuṇḍa lies just north of Dāvānala-kuṇḍa, near the terraced houses at the edge of Kevārivana. The name means rest, and the accounts say the Vraja-vāsīs came here after Kṛṣṇa consumed the forest fire and slept soundly from exhaustion. Nearby, in a building with four studio suites, are the samādhis of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya, Rāmacandra Kavirāja, Hemalatā Ṭhākurāṇī and Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Viśrāma-tīrtha
summary: Viśrāma-tīrtha, also called Ādi-varāha-tīrtha, is a sacred bathing place on the bank of the Yamunā that the accounts say is a hundred times more sacred than the Ganges.
body: Viśrāma-tīrtha, also called Ādi-varāha-tīrtha, is a sacred bathing place on the bank of the Yamunā that the accounts say is a hundred times more sacred than the Ganges. Vajranābha established a temple here with the deities of Yamunā and Yamarāja. On Bhrātṛ-dvitīyā, brothers and sisters throng here to bathe to avoid repeated birth.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Viśrānti-tīrtha
summary: Viśrānti-tīrtha is another name for Viśrāma-ghāṭa, and tradition touched its waters and offered ārati to Yamunā-devī during his parikrama.
body: Viśrānti-tīrtha is another name for Viśrāma-ghāṭa, and tradition touched its waters and offered ārati to Yamunā-devī during his parikrama. Tradition recalls Lord Varāha's statement to Bhūmi-devī about the potency of bathing there, which liberated a sinful brāhmaṇa turned Rākṣasa. They also mention Kaṁsa's funeral rites, performed with water from this tīrtha, and Jāhnavā-devī's visit to Viśrānti.

title: Viśvanātha-kuñja
summary: Viśvanātha-kuñja is the place near the Yoga-pīṭha where the body of Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura was placed in samādhi after he left this world in 1708.
body: Viśvanātha-kuñja is the place near the Yoga-pīṭha where the body of Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura was placed in samādhi after he left this world in 1708. He had worshipped a small Deity of Kṛṣṇa called Gokulānanda and performed bhajana here. In 1951 his samādhi was moved to the compound of the Rādhā-Gokulānanda temple.

title: Viśākhā-kuṇḍa
summary: Viśākhā-kuṇḍa is a pond in Nidhuvana that Kṛṣṇa created by poking the ground with His flute when Viśākhā complained of thirst during an outing with the gopīs.
body: Viśākhā-kuṇḍa is a pond in Nidhuvana that Kṛṣṇa created by poking the ground with His flute when Viśākhā complained of thirst during an outing with the gopīs. Tradition says that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa bathed here in Viśākhā-devī's grove, where rāsa dancing takes place at the rāsa-vedī platform nearby. The lake is now called Viśākhā-kuṇḍa, and the grove is where Uddhava was welcomed by the gopīs.

title: Viśākhānandada-kuñja
summary: Viśākhānandada-kuñja is the multicoloured grove of Viśākhā-devī, also called Madanānandada-kuñja because it is said to give Cupid bliss.
body: Viśākhānandada-kuñja is the multicoloured grove of Viśākhā-devī, also called Madanānandada-kuñja because it is said to give Cupid bliss. At its centre is a jewel-laden, sixteen-petalled lotus temple guarded by bumblebees, with four gates made of flowering vines. The grove lies on the northeastern bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa and is the object of Rati-mañjarī's meditations in Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī's writings.

title: Vraja-dhāma
summary: Vraja-dhāma is the holy land of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, and this is a guide to New Vraja-dhāma, the parikrama of its pastime places.
body: Vraja-dhāma is the holy land of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, and this is a guide to New Vraja-dhāma, the parikrama of its pastime places. Tradition dedicates the account to those devoted to Rādhā-Śyāmasundara and New Vraja-dhāma. The prosperity of New Vraja-dhāma depends on pleasing Rādhā-Śyāma through the service of Their devotees, and the syllable oṁ is its seed and support.

title: Vraja-grāma
summary: Vraja-grāma is mentioned mainly in passing, as a village Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through on His way from Reṇukā to Gokula.
body: Vraja-grāma is mentioned mainly in passing, as a village Caitanya Mahāprabhu passed through on His way from Reṇukā to Gokula. The account of Caitanya's travels is adapted from Caitanya-caritāmṛta. No further pastime is described at this village in the accounts.

title: Vṛndā-kuñja
summary: Vṛndā-kuñja is the tranquil grove that is the permanent residence of Vṛndā-devī, found in the secluded area near Nandagrāma.
body: Vṛndā-kuñja is the tranquil grove that is the permanent residence of Vṛndā-devī, found in the secluded area near Nandagrāma. From here she keeps groves and cottages throughout Vraja stocked with everything Kṛṣṇa needs for His pastimes, assisted by sylvan goddesses. Devotional accounts describe her as the choreographer of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, with Yogamāyā Paurṇamāsī-devī as their director.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vṛndā-kuṇḍa
summary: Vṛndā-kuṇḍa lies next to Gupta-kuṇḍa, opposite Akrūra-sthāna, and is the headquarters of Vraja's strategic command.
body: Vṛndā-kuṇḍa lies next to Gupta-kuṇḍa, opposite Akrūra-sthāna, and is the headquarters of Vraja's strategic command. Here Vṛndā-devī, Paurṇamāsī and Nāndīmukhī meet to plan Kṛṣṇa's daily itinerary. Tradition adds that it is the home of Vṛndā-devī's messenger, the parrot Dakṣa, who flies over Vṛndāvana and reports the day's events to her.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Vṛndāvana-dhāma
summary: Vṛndāvana-dhāma is the eternal abode of the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, and the accounts say the earthly Vṛndāvana-dhāma is always a representation of the original.
body: Vṛndāvana-dhāma is the eternal abode of the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, and the accounts say the earthly Vṛndāvana-dhāma is always a representation of the original. Bhauma Vṛndāvana is not under the jurisdiction of the material energy, and Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī is called the princess of Vṛndāvana-dhāma. Tradition mentions that the sage Mārkaṇḍeya came to Mārava-grāma to perform bhajana under the protection of Vṛndāvana-dhāma.

title: Vṛṣabhānu-kuṇḍa
summary: Vṛṣabhānu-kuṇḍa, also called Bhānu-sarovara, is a lake on the eastern border of Varṣāṇā where Mahārāja Vṛṣabhānu bathes each morning.
body: Vṛṣabhānu-kuṇḍa, also called Bhānu-sarovara, is a lake on the eastern border of Varṣāṇā where Mahārāja Vṛṣabhānu bathes each morning. Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī appeared either in Rāval or from a lotus in this lake. Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa enjoy water pastimes here, including hide-and-seek among the lotuses, and Kṛṣṇa secretly swims underwater to grab the feet of the gopīs.

title: Yamalārjuna-bhañjana-tīrtha
summary: Yamalārjuna-bhañjana-tīrtha is the place near the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa uprooted the twin arjuna trees.
body: Yamalārjuna-bhañjana-tīrtha is the place near the Yamunā where Kṛṣṇa uprooted the twin arjuna trees. It is associated with Mother Yaśodā churning yogurt on the veranda of Nanda's palace, now called Dadhi-manthana-sthala, and with her tying Kṛṣṇa in the courtyard below. These pastimes gave Kṛṣṇa the name Dāmodara.

title: Yamalārjuna-tīrtha
summary: Yamalārjuna-tīrtha is mentioned mainly as the starting point of the account covering the route from there to Rāval.
body: Yamalārjuna-tīrtha is mentioned mainly as the starting point of the account covering the route from there to Rāval. That account turns to Kṛṣṇa's butter-stealing pastimes and to Mother Yaśodā binding His belly with a rope, which made Him famous as Dāmodara. The place itself receives little further description.

title: Yamunā-tīra-vana
summary: Yamunā-tīra-vana is the forest along the banks of the Yamunā, where Kṛṣṇa spends day and night wandering by her shores, which earns Him the name Yamunā-tīra-vana-cārī.
body: Yamunā-tīra-vana is the forest along the banks of the Yamunā, where Kṛṣṇa spends day and night wandering by her shores, which earns Him the name Yamunā-tīra-vana-cārī. Devotional accounts describe how Yamunā melts her jewelled staircases and stills her fish and waterfowl at the sound of His flute. They also say Kṛṣṇa dances the rāsa dance on her banks and enjoys His water sports in her waves.

title: Yaśodā-kuṇḍa
summary: Yaśodā-kuṇḍa is a lake near Nandīśvara Hill where Mother Yaśodā bathes each morning, often with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma playing in the water.
body: Yaśodā-kuṇḍa is a lake near Nandīśvara Hill where Mother Yaśodā bathes each morning, often with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma playing in the water. The boys play in the groves around the lake and must be called back by Rohiṇī-devī, or by Yaśodā herself with a stick if they ignore her. Adjoining it is Nanda-kuṇḍa, where King Nanda bathes, and at the base of the hill is a cave used for bhajana.

title: Yoga-ghāṭa
summary: Yoga-ghāṭa is a site in Mathurā, east of Sudāmā's house, where the accounts say Kaṁsa tried to dash the eighth child of Devakī against a large rock.
body: Yoga-ghāṭa is a site in Mathurā, east of Sudāmā's house, where the accounts say Kaṁsa tried to dash the eighth child of Devakī against a large rock. That child was actually the Lord's Yogamāyā, born from Yaśodā and exchanged by Vasudeva for Kṛṣṇa. She slipped from Kaṁsa's grasp and rose into the air to mock him.

title: Yugala-ghāṭa
summary: Yugala-ghāṭa is a bathing place on the Yamunā past Sūrya-ghāṭa, named for the divine couple Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, who come here during daytime meetings to ease their fatigue and the heat.
body: Yugala-ghāṭa is a bathing place on the Yamunā past Sūrya-ghāṭa, named for the divine couple Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, who come here during daytime meetings to ease their fatigue and the heat. After bathing they dry off and go to a nearby grove at Vihāra-ghāṭa, where they decorate each other with fragrant flowers. The Yamunā's water here is so sweet that bees collect it.

summary: Yugala-kuṇḍa is mentioned mainly in passing, as one of the boundaries of the area around Nāradavana where the Vraja-vāsīs encamped during their exodus from Chaṭīkarā.
body: Yugala-kuṇḍa is mentioned mainly in passing, as one of the boundaries of the area around Nāradavana where the Vraja-vāsīs encamped during their exodus from Chaṭīkarā. title: Yugala-saṅgama-ghāṭa
summary: Yugala-saṅgama-ghāṭa is the walkway separating Rādhā-kuṇḍa from Śyāma-kuṇḍa, and at its centre is the meeting place (saṅgama) where the liquid forms of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa embrace.
body: Yugala-saṅgama-ghāṭa is the walkway separating Rādhā-kuṇḍa from Śyāma-kuṇḍa, and at its centre is the meeting place (saṅgama) where the liquid forms of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa embrace. Devotees are advised to bathe here first in Rādhā-kuṇḍa, then Śyāma-kuṇḍa, then Rādhā-kuṇḍa again. Nearby is Ratna-vedī, where Caraṇa-cihna marks the lotus footprints of Rādhā and Śyāmasundara.

title: Yāvavaṭa
summary: Yāvavaṭa is a banyan tree under which Kṛṣṇa painted Rādhā's feet with red lac (yāva), and the town of Yāvaṭā takes its name from it.
body: Yāvavaṭa is a banyan tree under which Kṛṣṇa painted Rādhā's feet with red lac (yāva), and the town of Yāvaṭā takes its name from it. It is listed among the sixteen banyan trees of Vraja and the area is said to hold fifteen sacred kuṇḍas marking major pastime places of the divine couple. The truths of these Yāvaṭā pastimes are described as concealed from ordinary men.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places

title: Yāvaṭā-grāma
summary: Yāvaṭā-grāma is the village named after the Yāvavaṭa banyan tree, where Lalitā was married to Bhairava-gopa.
body: Yāvaṭā-grāma is the village named after the Yāvavaṭa banyan tree, where Lalitā was married to Bhairava-gopa. Tradition describes a pastime at nearby Kokilavana, where Kṛṣṇa, who can imitate the black cuckoo's call, secretly enlisted the birds' help. The area is also linked to Lalitā's ancestral home at Ūñchagaon and to the festival held at Lalitā-vivāha-sthala.
source_ref: User-provided notes on Vraja holy places
